Know that profit in a corrupt partnership is according to the amount of capital if it is a capital partnership, and according to the work if it is a labor partnership; this is clear. A partnership is annulled by the death of one of the two.

As for the detailed classification of partnership types in the school of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, they are likewise of two kinds: partnership of ownership (shirkat amlak) and partnership of contract (shirkat 'uqud).

Partnership of contract according to the Hanbalis is of five types: partnership of inan, of bodies, of reputation, of mudaraba, and of comprehensive (mufawada).

As for partnership of bodies, it is permitted according to them, whether the work is among crafts or the acquisition of permissible resources. If the work is unified, it is permitted according to them without disagreement. If the work differs, Abu al-Khattab said: it is not permitted, in agreement with the Malikis; and al-Qadi said: it is permitted, in agreement with the Hanafis (p-245) in crafts but not in the acquisition of permissible resources.

If the two agree that one of them undertakes the work and the second performs it, with the wage shared between them, the partnership is valid according to the Hanbalis and the Hanafis, in contrast to Zufar. The profit in partnership of bodies is according to what they agreed upon, according to the Hanbalis.

As for partnership of reputation, which we previously mentioned is known among the Malikis as "shirkat al-dhimam," it is also permitted in the school of Imam Ahmad, in agreement with Abu Hanifa and in contrast to Malik and al-Shafi'i. As for partnership of inan, it is also permitted according to Imam Ahmad, and we have previously mentioned the consensus on its permissibility. According to them, it is that two men partner with their two properties, on the condition that they work with their bodies in them, and the profit is between them. This partnership, according to them, is permitted only in dinars and dirhams, and not in goods.

As for comprehensive partnership, according to the Hanbalis it is of two kinds: one permitted and the other prohibited.

The permitted kind is that the two partner in all types of partnership, such as combining inan, reputation, and bodies, and this is valid because each type is valid on its own, so it is valid together with others.

And as for the type of partnership they prohibit: it is that the two partners include in the partnership the sharing of whatever each of them acquires through inheritance, or finds as buried treasure (*rikaz*) or as lost property (*luqatah*), and that each of them becomes liable for what the other is liable for, such as the compensation for a crime (*arsh jinayah*), liability for usurpation (*ghasb*), the value of something destroyed, the payment for a guarantee, and suretyship. The invalidity of this type is evident because of the uncertainty (*gharar*) it contains, as you see.

As for *shirkat al-mudarabah*, which is *qiradh*, it is permissible according to all scholars. We have already mentioned that it is: that one person gives another money to trade with, on the condition that the profit is shared between them in a ratio they agree upon. That the profit in *mudarabah* follows what they agreed upon is not disputed among the scholars, whether it is half, less, or more, for the owner of the capital or for the worker.

As for *shirkat al-'inan* according to the Shafi'is, the Hanbalis, the Hanafis and the Malikis, and *shirkat al-mufawadah* according to the Malikis, there is disagreement regarding the ratio of profit. Malik and al-Shafi'i held that profit and loss must be in proportion to the two capitals. Abu Hanifah and Ahmad held that the profit between them is according to what they agreed upon, so they may be equal in profit even though the capitals differ.

The argument of the first view is that profit follows capital, so it must be in proportion to it. The argument of the latter view is that work is something by which profit is earned, and one of them may be more skilled in trade and more capable of work than the other, so his share is increased for the increase in his work.

This is the summary of the positions of the four Imams regarding the types of partnership. You have learned that they unanimously agreed on the permissibility of *shirkat al-'inan*, *shirkat al-mudarabah*, and *shirkat al-amlak* (partnership in ownership), and they differed regarding other types. The Hanafis and Hanbalis permitted *shirkat al-wujuh* (partnership based on reputation and credit), while the Malikis and Shafi'is prohibited it.

The Malikis, Hanafis and Hanbalis permitted *shirkat al-abdan* (partnership of labor) except in the acquisition of permissible things only; the Hanafis did not permit it, while the Shafi'is prohibited *shirkat al-abdan* absolutely.

The Malikis permitted *shirkat al-mufawadah* and depicted it in a manner different from that of the other schools. The Hanbalis permitted a type of *mufawadah* and depicted it in a form different from how others depicted it. The Shafi'is prohibited *mufawadah* as they prohibited *shirkat al-abdan* and *al-wujuh*, and they depicted *mufawadah* in another form as previously mentioned.

The Shafi'is permit partnership with fungible (*mithli*) goods absolutely, whether currency or otherwise, but not with non-fungible (*muqawwamat*) goods.

The Hanafis permit it only with the two currencies (gold and silver), bullion, and circulating coins. The Hanbalis permit it only with dinars and dirhams. All of this has been mentioned previously.

We have explained the legal device (*hilah*) for partnership with commodities according to the Shafi'is and Hanafis. According to the Malikis, it is permissible with dinars from each of them, with dirhams from each of them, with dinars and dirhams from each of them, with cash from one and goods from the other, or with goods from each of them, whether they agree or differ. It was said: only if they agree, not if they differ, except that goods must be valued. As for mixing the two capitals, it is necessary according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, so that neither can be distinguished from the other, as previously mentioned. In the Maliki school, it suffices that the two capitals be in one place of safekeeping, and even if each of the two capitals is in its own bag, without mixing with the other, that is sufficient. Mixing of the two capitals is not a condition according to the Hanafis, as previously mentioned, and likewise it is not a condition according to the Hanbalis.

Thus it results that only the Shafi'is require mixing the two capitals, while the Malikis require only that the two capitals be in one location, such as a shop or a chest, even if each of them is distinct from the other.

Having learned the summary of the scholars' words on the types of partnership, we will mention what is available of their evidences. As for the type that the Malikis call *mufawadah* and that the Shafi'is and Hanbalis express as *shirkat al-'inan*, evidence may be drawn for it from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, which we previously cited from al-Bukhari and Imam Ahmad, for it indicates partnership in trade, buying and selling, because the purpose of partnership is mutual cooperation in the work mentioned, so each of the two partners stands in for the other. The hadith of Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet, also supports this, where he said: Allah says, "I am the third of the two partners..." the hadith mentioned earlier. We have explained the scholars' words regarding it and shown that it is fit for use as evidence, and it is clear that the two work together with the partnership capital, as indicated by his saying: "as long as neither of them betrays the other..." the hadith.

Also supporting this is the hadith of al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib mentioned earlier, that he was a partner of the Prophet (ﷺ) as previously mentioned, and that is a partnership in trade, buying and selling.

As for *shirkat al-abdan*, evidence for it is taken from what Abu 'Ubaydah narrated from his father 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I, 'Ammar and Sa'd formed a partnership in what we would obtain on the day of Badr. He said: Sa'd came with two prisoners, while I and 'Ammar came with nothing." Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. Al-Majd said in *Muntaqa al-Akhbar* after citing it: "It is a proof for partnership of labor and the acquisition of permissible things." This hadith has been criticized on the grounds that Abu 'Ubaydah did not hear from his father 'Abdullah mentioned, so the hadith is *mursal* (with a missing link). We have mentioned many times that the three Imams take *mursal* as evidence, unlike the hadith scholars.

As for *mudarabah*, no sound hadith traced to the Prophet has been established regarding it, but the Companions unanimously agreed upon it because of its prevalence and spread among them without objection. The practice of the Muslims concerning it has continued from the time of the Companions until now without objection. Ibn Hazm said in *Maratib al-Ijma'* (The Levels of Consensus): "Every chapter of jurisprudence has a basis in the Book and the Sunnah, except *qiradh* (*mudarabah*). We have found no basis for it in either of them at all, but it is a sound consensus by itself. What is certain is that it existed in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), he knew of it and approved it, for otherwise it would not have been permissible." End of quotation via al-Shawkani's transmission in *Nayl al-Awtar*.

Know that the differences of the Imams that we mentioned regarding the types of partnership mentioned return to a difference in *tahqiq al-manat* (determining the effective cause). Some say: this form contains *gharar* (uncertainty), which is the cause for prohibition, so it is prohibited. Another says: there is no *gharar* in this form that necessitates prohibition, so the cause for prohibition is not present in it. And Allah knows best.

The third issue: some Maliki scholars and others also derived from this noble verse that is our present subject: the permissibility of travelling companions pooling their food and eating together, even if some of them eat more than others, because the People of the Cave sent their silver to buy food for them to eat all together. We have previously cited from Ibn al-'Arabi that it is possible that each one's silver and food were separate, so the verse does not indicate that they pooled their food, just as we previously quoted from him that it does not indicate partnership because of that possibility. It has a basis, as you see.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: "There is no reliance in this matter except on two hadiths. One is that Ibn 'Umar passed by people eating dates, and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade *iqran* (combining two dates in one bite) unless a man seeks his companion's permission. The second is the hadith of Abu 'Ubaydah concerning the army of *al-Khabat* (leaves), and this is less evident than the first, because it is possible that Abu 'Ubaydah gave them just enough of that provision and did not pool it." End of the words of Ibn al-'Arabi, the Maliki, may Allah have mercy on him.

The author of these notes, may Allah pardon him, says: This type of partnership, which is the pooling of travelling companions' food and their sharing in eating it, is known as *nihd* (with the *nun* either vowelled with kasra or fatha). Its permissibility has evidence from the Book and the Sunnah. As for the evidence from the Book, it is the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿And if you mix with them, they are your brothers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220], for it indicates mixing the food of an orphan with the food of his guardian and both eating together. And His words, Exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon you to eat together or separately﴾ [al-Nur: 61]. Among the forms of eating together is that the food is shared between them and they all eat together. As for the Sunnah, authentic hadiths indicate this, among them the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment to the coast and appointed Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah over them; they were three hundred men, and I was among them. We set out until, when we were in part of the way, the provisions ran out. Abu 'Ubaydah ordered that the provisions of that army be gathered, and all of it was gathered; it was two saddlebags of dates. He would ration us a little each day until it ran out, so we got only one date each. I said: What use is one date? He said: We found its loss when it ran out. Then we reached the sea, and there was a whale..." The hadith. This hadith is established in the *Sahih*, and the wording we cited is that of al-Bukhari in the Book of *Shirkah*. In it Abu 'Ubaydah gathered the remaining provisions of the people and mixed them into two saddlebags of dates, and he was not rebuked for it by the Prophet (ﷺ) after their arrival to him.

Among them is the hadith of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The provisions of the people ran low and they became destitute, so they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking to slaughter their camels, and he permitted them. Then 'Umar met them and they informed him, and he said: What will remain for you after your camels? He entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, what will remain for them after their camels? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Call out to the people, and they will bring the surplus of their provisions.' So a leather cloth was spread out, and they placed it on the cloth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood, supplicated and blessed it, then called them with their containers, and the people took handfuls until they finished. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah.'" This hadith is established in the *Sahih*, and the wording we cited is also al-Bukhari's in the Book of *Shirkah*, and in it: he mixed their food, some with the rest.

Among them is the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade a man to combine two dates together until he seeks permission from his companions." In a narration in the *Sahih*, the Prophet (ﷺ) "forbade *iqran* unless one of you seeks his brother's permission."

All of this is established in the *Sahih*, and the wording is that of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, in the Book of *Shirkah*. The companion's permission to him indicates their partnership in the dates, as you see. This permissibility that we mentioned, of travelling companions pooling their food and all eating from it, is what al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, meant by the term *nihd* in his words in the Book of *Shirkah*: "Partnership in food and *nihd*..." up to his words: "The Muslims saw no harm in *nihd*, that this one eats some, and this one some, and this one some," etc.

Branches related to the issue of partnership:

The first: If a person gives his riding animal to another to work with it, and what Allah provides is shared between them in halves, or thirds, or however they stipulate, then there is disagreement among scholars about the validity of this. Some said it is valid, and this is the view of Imam Ahmad; something similar is reported from al-Awza'i. Others said it is not valid, and whatever is earned belongs to the worker, and he owes the usual rental value (*ajrat mithl*) of the animal. This is the view of Malik. Ibn Qudamah said in *al-Mughni*: al-Hasan and al-Nakha'i disliked this. Al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, Ibn al-Mundhir and the people of opinion (*ashab al-ra'y*) said: it is not valid, and all the profit belongs to the owner of the animal, and the worker has the usual wage for his work. This is the essence of the words of the scholars on this issue.

[p. 250]

The strongest of the opinions in this matter, in my view, is the position of those who permit it, such as Imam Ahmad, based on the hadith of Ruwayfi' ibn Thabit, who said: "In the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), one of us would take the worn-out mount of his brother on the condition that he has half of what is taken as booty and we have half. And one of us would have only the arrowhead and feathers (of an arrow) flown for him while the other had the shaft." This hadith was narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i. Al-Shawkani said in *Nayl al-Awtar*: "The isnad of Abu Dawud includes Shayban ibn Umayya al-Qitbani, who is unknown (majhul), but the rest of its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat). Al-Nasa'i narrated it through a route other than this unknown narrator, with an isnad all of whose narrators are trustworthy." The hadith is a clear proof for the permissibility of one man giving another his riding animal for jihad on the condition that the spoils are shared between them, and this is a work on the animal in return for the condition that what God grants them is shared between them, as you see. The distinction between work in jihad and work outside it does not appear clearly. And God knows best.

The second branch: three parties partner, one providing an animal, another providing the (skilled) labor of... [the text reads: "ومِن آخَرَ رِوايَةٌ"]. Specifically, one provides an animal, another provides a water-skin (riwayah), and the third provides the work, on the condition that whatever God grants them is shared among them. Is this permissible? Scholars have differed on this. Some said it is not permissible, and this is the position of Malik and the apparent view of al-Shafi'i. Among those who held this is the judge (al-Qadi) from the Hanbalis, while some Hanbalis permitted it. Ibn Qudamah said in *al-Mughni*: "It is valid according to the analogy of Ahmad's view, may God have mercy on him."

The third branch: four parties partner, one providing a shop (dukkan), another a millstone (rahan), another a mule (baghl), and the fourth the work, on the condition that they grind with these, and whatever God grants them is shared among them. Is this valid or not? Scholars differed. It was said that it is valid, and this is the position of Imam Ahmad. The judge from the Hanbalis disagreed, in agreement with those who prohibit it, such as the Malikis. Ibn Qudamah said: "Prohibiting it is the apparent view of al-Shafi'i, because this cannot be a partnership (musharakah) or a profit-sharing contract (mudarabah). If the owner of the millstone, the owner of the animal, and the owner of the shop agreed to all work, and the rent of the shop, the millstone, and the animal were equal, and the labor of their owners were equal, it is permissible according to the Malikis." This is the matter to which Khalil pointed in his *Mukhtasar* with his words, linking it to what is not permitted: "and the owner of a millstone, the owner of a house, and the owner of an animal, so that they may know if the rents are not equal and they are equal in the yield, and they return the rentals; and if it is stipulated that the owner of the animal works, the yield is his and the rents of both are upon him."

It is not hidden that *al-shirkah* (partnership) is a major chapter of jurisprudence (fiqh), and that its issues are explained exhaustively in the books of the furu' (derivative rulings) of the four Imams, may God be pleased with them all. Our aim here is to show its permissibility by the Book, the Sunnah, and ijma' (scholarly consensus), and to mention its divisions and its linguistic and technical meanings, the disagreement of scholars concerning it, the explanation of their views, and the mention of some of its branches as a reminder of others. We have covered all of that, and praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, if they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you or return you to their religion, and you will never succeed thereafter.﴾

In this noble verse, exalted and majestic is He, He mentions concerning the People of the Cave that they said: their people, the disbelievers, from whom they had fled with their religion, if they gain the upper hand over them, that is, come to know of them and learn their whereabouts, will stone them with rocks, and that is among the most hideous kinds of killing. It was also said: they will stone them with abuse and slander. "Or return you to their religion" means: bring you back to the religion of disbelief.

What He mentions here, of the disbelievers' conduct toward the Muslims, namely harm or forcing them back to disbelief, He mentions in other places as being the conduct of the disbelievers toward the messengers and their followers (p-251):

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely expel you from our land or you will return to our religion."﴾ [Ibrahim: 13],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believed with you from our city, or you will return to our religion." He said, "Even though we were unwilling? We would have invented against Allah a lie if we returned to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. And it would not be for us to return to it unless Allah wills."﴾ to the end of the verse [Al-A'raf: 88-89],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 217],

along with other verses.

* *

Question

Some scholars took from this noble verse that excuse by coercion is a distinctive feature of this Ummah, because His saying concerning the People of the Cave: ﴿if they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you or return you to their religion﴾ [Al-Kahf: 20], is apparent in their being compelled to that and their not being willing, yet He said of them: ﴿and you will never succeed thereafter﴾, which shows that such coercion is not an excuse. This meaning is supported by the hadith of Tariq ibn Shihab concerning the man who entered the Fire over a fly, which he brought near under coercion through fear of being killed, because his companion who refused to bring near even a fly was killed.

It is also supported by the indication of the discourse (dalil al-khitab), i.e., the concept of contrary implication (mafhum al-mukhalafa) in His saying ﷺ: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for me from my Ummah the error, the forgetting, and what they have been compelled to do" (ﷺ). For it is understood from his saying, "has overlooked for me from my Ummah," that other nations were not granted that overlooking. And although Imam Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim criticized this hadith, scholars, early and late, received it with acceptance, and it has firm corroborations in the Noble Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah. We have clarified this matter in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book), in surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Indeed, if they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you﴾ and so on [Al-Kahf: 20]; therefore we have abridged it here. As for this Ummah, Allah, exalted is He, has expressly stated their excuse by coercion in His saying: ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart is firm in faith﴾ [An-Nahl: 106]. And Allah knows best.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-330) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah al-Kahf

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, if they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you or return you to their religion, and you will never succeed thereafter.﴾

This verse, by its apparent meaning, indicates that one who is compelled to disbelief will never succeed.

Another verse has come indicating that one compelled to disbelief is excused if his heart is firm in faith, namely His saying: ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart is firm in faith. But whoever opens his breast to disbelief﴾ [An-Nahl: 106].

The answer to this is in two respects:

The first: The lifting of blame under coercion is a distinctive feature of this Ummah, and it is included in His saying: ﴿and He removes from them their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾ [Al-A'raf: 157]. The saying of the Prophet ﷺ indicates this: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for me from my Ummah the error, the forgetting, and what they have been compelled to do," so it indicates by its implied meaning its specificity to his Ummah (ﷺ).

This is not a mafhum al-laqab (implication from a proper name), because the basis of the specification is its being characterized by superiority over those before him among the messengers, and its Ummah's characterization by it over those before them among the nations. Although Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim criticized the hadith, scholars, early and late, received it with acceptance. Among the clearest proofs that those before us had no excuse by coercion is the hadith of Tariq ibn Shihab concerning the man who entered the Fire over a fly which he brought near to an idol, although he brought it near in order to free himself from the evil of the idol-worshippers, and his companion who refused to do that was killed; so he knew that if he did not do it, they would kill him as they killed his companion. There is no greater coercion than fear of death, and yet he entered the Fire and coercion did not benefit him. The apparent meanings of the verses indicate this. His saying: "and you will never succeed thereafter" is apparent in their not succeeding under coercion, because His saying: ﴿they will stone you or return you to their religion﴾ is explicit in (p-331) coercion. And His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 286], together with His saying, "I have done so," as established in Sahih Muslim, indicates by its apparent meaning that the obligation of that was known before. And His saying: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot﴾ [Ta-Ha: 115], together with His saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord﴾ [Ta-Ha: 121], attributing to him forgetting and disobedience together, also indicates this. And according to the view that the intended meaning of forgetting is abandonment, there is no proof in the verse.

His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make mistakes﴾, together with His saying: ﴿as You placed it upon those before us﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 286], and this is supported by what al-Baghawi mentioned in his tafsir from al-Kalbi, that taking to task for forgetting was among the burdens upon those before us, and its punishment was hastened for them in this world, so some good things were forbidden to them. Some scholars said: coercion is an excuse for those before us, and according to this the answer is:

The second respect: Coercion to disbelief may be a cause for Satan to lure one into approving of it and persisting in it, as is understood from the implied meaning of His saying: ﴿while his heart is firm in faith﴾ [An-Nahl: 106]. To this respect inclined the author of Ruh al-Ma'ani. The first is more apparent and clearer to me, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who prevailed over their affair said, "We will surely take over them a place of worship."﴾

Allah does not specify here who these people were who prevailed over their affair: were they among the Muslims or among the disbelievers? Ibn Jarir and others mention two opinions concerning them: the first is that they were disbelievers, and the second is that they were Muslims. (p-252) The evidence for the second is their saying: ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾ [al-Kahf: 21], because the taking of places of worship (masajid) is one of the attributes of the believers, not of the disbelievers. So said some of the people of knowledge. But one may say: taking places of worship over graves is an act of those cursed upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), not an act of the Muslims. We have already presented this fully, with its evidence, in Surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the companions of al-Hijr did deny the messengers﴾ and the verse that follows [al-Hijr: 80].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "They were three, the fourth of them being their dog," and they will say, "They were five, the sixth of them being their dog," guessing at the unseen; and they will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog." Say, "My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few."﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted informs us about the disagreement of people concerning the number of the Companions of the Cave. He mentions three opinions, indicating that there is no fourth opinion. The noble verse contains an indication that the third opinion is the correct one, and that the first two are false. For when He mentioned the first two opinions with His saying, ﴿They will say, "They were three, the fourth of them being their dog," and they will say, "They were five, the sixth of them being their dog"﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-Kahf: 22], He followed this with His saying, ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾, meaning: speaking without knowledge, like one who throws toward a place he does not know, for he is hardly likely to hit it, and even if he hits it, it is without intention. This is like His saying: ﴿And they hurl (their words) at the unseen from a distant place﴾ [Saba: 53].

Al-Qurtubi said: "Al-rajm (guessing) is speaking on the basis of conjecture. It is said of everything that is guessed at: rujima fihi, and it is marjum and murajjam, as Zuhayr said:

"And war is only what you have known and tasted, and he is not one to speak of it in guesses (al-murajjam)."

Then He related the third opinion with His saying, ﴿And they will say, "They were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog"﴾, and He affirmed it, and did not mention after it that this is guessing at the unseen. This indicates that it is the correct one. As for His saying, ﴿none knows them except a few﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: "I am among that few who know them; they were seven."

And His saying, ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best their number"﴾, contains a teaching for people that they should refer the knowledge of things back to their Creator, may He be exalted, even if they know them, just as He informed His Prophet ﷺ of the duration of their stay in His saying: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾ [Al-Kahf: 25]. Then He commanded him, despite that, to refer the knowledge back to Him, may He be exalted, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Allah knows best how long they remained." To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-Kahf: 26].

What we have mentioned, that there is no fourth opinion, was stated by Ibn Kathir, taking it from the apparent meaning of the noble verse. However, Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Juraij said: they were eight. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,"﴾ ﴿unless [you add], "If Allah wills."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah forbade His Prophet ﷺ from saying that he would do something in the future except by making it conditional upon the will (mashi'ah) of Allah, Who—exalted is He—nothing in the universe comes to pass, whatever it may be, except by His will. So His saying, ﴿And never say of anything﴾ [al-Kahf: 23], means: do not say, concerning something you resolve to do in the future, "Indeed, I will do that thing tomorrow."

By "tomorrow" is meant the time that is yet to come, not specifically the next day. Among the idioms of Arabic is the use of "tomorrow" (ghad) to denote the future; from it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"I know the knowledge of today and of the yesterday before it, but concerning the knowledge of what is in tomorrow, I am blind."

He means that he does not know what will happen in the future, since there is no reason to restrict that to one particular day.

His saying, ﴿unless [you add], "If Allah wills."﴾ [al-Kahf: 24], means: unless you are saying, "unless Allah wills," that is, making it dependent upon the will of Allah; or, do not say it except with "If Allah wills," that is, except by the will of Allah. The phrase is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: except while connected to the will of Allah, saying "If Allah wills." This was stated by az-Zamakhshari and others.

The occasion of revelation (sabab nuzul) of this noble verse: "The Jews said to the Quraysh: Ask Muhammad ﷺ about the Spirit (ruh), about a man who traveled the earth (they meant Dhul-Qarnayn), and about youths who had a wondrous story in past times (they meant the People of the Cave). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: 'I will inform you tomorrow about what you asked,' and he did not say, 'If Allah wills.' So revelation was withheld from him for a period, said to be fifteen nights, and said to be otherwise. This grieved him, the delay of revelation from him. Then Allah revealed to him the answer to the three questions. Regarding the Spirit: ﴿They ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is of the command of my Lord﴾ [al-Isra': 85], and regarding the youths: ﴿We relate to you their story in truth﴾ [al-Kahf: 13] and the verses that follow to the end of their story, and regarding the wandering man: ﴿They ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say: I will recite to you of him a mention﴾ [al-Kahf: 83] and the verses to the end of his story."

When you know the meaning of this noble verse and its occasion of revelation, and that Allah reproached His Prophet in it for not saying "If Allah wills" when he said to them, "I will inform you tomorrow," then know that another verse, together with the explanation of the Sunnah relating to it, indicates that Allah reproached His Prophet Sulayman for not saying "If Allah wills," just as He reproached His Prophet in this verse for that. Indeed, the trial of Sulayman through that was even more severe. For al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Sulayman ibn Dawud, upon him and upon our Prophet be blessings and peace, said: 'Tonight I will go around to seventy women—and in another narration ninety women, and in another a hundred women—each of whom will bear a boy who will fight in the way of Allah.' It was said to him—and in another narration the angel said to him—'Say: If Allah wills.' But he did not say it. So he went around to them, and none of them bore a child except one woman, who bore half a human being." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, had he said 'If Allah wills,' he would not have broken his oath, and it would have been a means of attaining his need." And in another narration: "And they would have fought in the way of Allah as horsemen, all of them." End of quotation.

When you know this, know that this sound hadith explains the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did try Solomon and We placed upon his throne a body﴾ [Sad: 34] and the verse, and that the trial of Sulayman was because of his leaving the saying "If Allah wills," and that he fathered from those women only one, who was half a human being, and that this body which is half a human being is what was placed upon his throne after his death, in His saying: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾ and the verse. As for what the commentators mention in explaining His saying, ﴿And We did try Solomon﴾ and the verse, of the story of the devil who took the ring and sat on Solomon's throne and drove Solomon from his kingdom, until he found the ring in the belly of the fish which had been given to him by one who worked for him for wages, while Solomon was driven from his kingdom, to the end of the story: it is clear that this is false, without basis, and unfitting to the station of prophethood. It is among the Isra'iliyyat, whose falsehood is not hidden.

The apparent meaning of the verse is what we have mentioned, and the Sahih Sunnah indicates it in general terms, and some verifying scholars have chosen it. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 24:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾.

Regarding this noble verse, there are two well-known opinions among the scholars of tafsir (exegesis):

The first: this noble verse is connected to what precedes it, and the meaning is: if you say, "I will do such-and-such tomorrow," and you forget to say, "If God wills" (in shā' Allāh), and then you remember after that, then say, "If God wills"; that is, remember your Lord by making what you say, that you will do it tomorrow, contingent upon His will, when you remember after forgetting. This opinion is the apparent one, because the Most High's words before it indicate it: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [when adding], "If Allah wills"﴾ [al-Kahf: 23-24]. It is the opinion of the majority. Among those who held it were Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu al-'Aliyah, and others.

The second opinion: the verse has no connection to what precedes it, and the meaning is: when forgetfulness befalls you concerning something, then remember God, because forgetfulness is from Satan, as the Most High said concerning the servant of Musa: ﴿And none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it﴾ [al-Kahf: 63]. Similarly His saying: ﴿Satan has overcome them and caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Mujadila: 19]. The Most High also said: ﴿And if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-An'am: 68]. The remembrance of God repels Satan, as the Most High's words indicate: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 36]. And His saying: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws﴾ [an-Nas: 1-4] — that is, the whisperer at the time of heedlessness of the remembrance of God; al-Khannas is the one who withdraws and retreats in humiliation at the remembrance of God. So when Satan departs, forgetfulness departs. Some have said: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ [al-Kahf: 24] means: pray the prayer you were forgetful of when you remember it, as the Most High said: ﴿And establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ [Ta-Ha: 14]. As for the view of one who said "when you forget" means "when you become angry," it is clearly weak.

* *

Issue

It is widely reported on the tongues of scholars from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) that he derived from this noble verse that the exception (istithna') is valid even when its utterance is delayed from the thing excepted for a long time. Some said: up to a month; some said: up to a year; and some reported from him: the exception is permissible at any time. The basis for his deriving this from the verse was: Allah the Most High forbade His Prophet to say that he would do something in the future without the exception of "if Allah wills," then He said: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾; that is, if you forget to add "if Allah wills," then make the exception when you remember, without restriction by immediacy or proximity.

The verified truth beyond doubt is that the exception is valid only when joined to what is excepted from, and that a delayed exception has no effect and does not dissolve an oath. Had a delayed exception been valid, it would never be known in this world that any contract or oath had been established, or anything else, since there would always be the possibility that an exception might come afterward; and this is utterly false, as you see. It is related from al-Mansur that he was informed that Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) opposed the aforementioned view of Ibn 'Abbas; so he summoned him to rebuke him for it. Imam Abu Hanifa said to al-Mansur: "This rebounds upon you! You take the pledge of allegiance by oaths. Would you be content that they leave your presence and make an exception, and then rise against you?!" He admired his words and was pleased with him.

* *

Benefit

Ibn al-'Arabi al-Maliki said: I heard a girl in Baghdad say to her neighbour: "If the view of Ibn 'Abbas concerning the exception were correct, Allah would not have said to Ayyub: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath﴾ [Sad: 44]; rather He would have said, 'Make the exception, if Allah wills.'" This was concluded from him through the transmission of the author of Nashr al-Bunud in his commentary, and from his saying in Maraqi as-Su'ud:

"By partnership and by premeditation, some held [it valid]; but one required that it be joined.
And in other cases, apart from necessity, and it is void by silence for remembrance."

If it is asked: what is the correct answer regarding what is attributed to Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) about the validity of the delayed exception?

The answer: Ibn 'Abbas's meaning (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) is that Allah rebuked His Prophet for his saying that he would do such-and-such tomorrow without saying "if Allah wills," and He made clear to him that the contingency upon the will of Allah is what should be done, since nothing occurs except by His will. So if one forgets to make the contingency upon the will, then remembers, even after a long time, he should say "if Allah wills," in order to be free of the obligation of not having made the contingency upon the will, and to have entrusted the matter to One by whose will alone things occur. The result of this exception is thus the discharge of the burden of abandoning what necessitated the earlier rebuke, not that it dissolves the oath, since its remedy has already passed by the separation. This is the meaning of Ibn 'Abbas, as al-Tabari and others affirmed, and there is no prohibition or difficulty in it.

Some scholars gave another answer, namely: that he intended the exception in his heart and forgot to utter it with his tongue, so he then expressed the exception he had intended at the time of the oath. So said some of them; but the first is the apparent one, and knowledge is with Allah the Most High.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 26 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth.﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, explains that He alone is singled out with the knowledge of the unseen in the heavens and the earth. He mentions this meaning in many verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Say, "None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah. And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."﴾ [an-Naml: 65],
• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted.﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 9],
• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. And Allah would not inform you of the unseen...﴾ to the end of the verse [Ali 'Imran: 179],
• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the matter will all be returned...﴾ to the end of the verse [Hud: 123], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, and not a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but that it is in a clear register.﴾ [al-An'am: 59], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear register.﴾ [Yunus: 61], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Knower of the unseen, from whom is not absent an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth, nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but that it is in a clear register.﴾ [Saba': 3], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah – nothing on the earth or in the heaven is hidden from Him.﴾

And He explains in other places that He informs whomever He wills of His creation of whatever He wills of His revelation, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Knower of the unseen, so He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved...﴾ to the end of the verses [al-Jinn: 26–27]. He alluded to this by His saying:

• ﴿And Allah would not inform you of the unseen, but Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 179],

and to other verses besides these.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿See how Hearing and Seeing He is!﴾

That is: how seeing He is and how hearing He is, exalted is He. What He mentions in this noble verse of His being described with hearing and sight, He also mentions in other places, such as His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ [ash-Shura: 11], and His saying: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your conversation. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ [al-Mujadila: 1], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ [al-Hajj: 75]. The verses on this are very numerous.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They have not besides Him any guardian.﴾

In this noble verse He mentions that the People of the Cave have no guardian besides Him, exalted is He; rather, He is their guardian, exalted is He. This meaning is mentioned in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the guardian of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of Allah – there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [Yunus: 62]. So He explains that He is the guardian (wali) of the believers, and that the believers are His allies. The wali (guardian, ally) is the one between whom and you there is a bond by which he takes your side and you take his side. Faith is the bond by which the believers take their Lord's side through obedience, and by which He takes their side through reward, victory and help.

He explains in other places that the believers are allies of one another, such as His saying: ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 55], and His saying: ﴿The believing men and believing women are allies of one another...﴾ to the end of the verse [at-Tawbah: 71], and He explains in other places that our Prophet ﷺ is closer to the believers than their own selves, as in His saying: ﴿The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 6].

He explains in another place that He, exalted is He, is the Patron (mawla) of the believers and not of the disbelievers, as in His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the protector of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector.﴾ [Muhammad: 11]. This guardianship specific to the believers is the guardianship of reward, victory, success and help, and it does not contradict His being the Patron (mawla) of the disbelievers in the sense of guardianship of sovereignty, dominance, authority and will, such as His saying: ﴿And they are returned to Allah, their true Master, and lost from them is what they used to invent.﴾ [Yunus: 30]. Some scholars said: the pronoun in His saying ﴿They have not besides Him any guardian﴾ refers to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth understood from His saying ﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾. It was said: the pronoun in His saying "they have" refers to the disbelievers contemporary with the Prophet ﷺ; this was mentioned by al-Qurtubi. In any case, the preceding verses indicate that the guardianship of all belongs to their Creator, exalted is He, and that among it is the guardianship of reward, success and help, and the guardianship of sovereignty, dominance, authority and will. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He does not share His command with anyone.﴾

Most of the seven readers, except Ibn 'Amir, read this letter "wa-la yushriku" with the yaa' (third person, masculine) and a damma on the kaf, as a statement, with "la" as a negation. The meaning: Allah, exalted is He, does not make anyone a partner in His command; rather, command belongs to Him alone, exalted is He, and there is no command for anyone else whatsoever. So what is lawful is what He made lawful, what is unlawful is what He made unlawful, the religion is what He legislated, and the decree is what He decreed. Ibn 'Amir, of the seven, read "wa-la tushrik" with a damma on the taa' (second person) and a sukun on the kaf, in the form of a prohibition, meaning: do not make anyone a partner, O Prophet of Allah, or do not make anyone a partner, O addressee, in the command of Allah, exalted is He; rather, purify the command for Allah from any taint of associating others with Him in command. His command, exalted is He, mentioned in His saying ﴿And He does not share His command with anyone﴾ encompasses everything He decrees, and legislation enters into this first and foremost.

What this noble verse contains, that command belongs to Allah alone with no partner in it, is established in both readings, and it is explained in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The decision is only for Allah. He has commanded that you worship none but Him﴾ [Yusuf: 40], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The decision is only for Allah. In Him I have put my trust﴾ to the end of the verse [Yusuf: 67], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is to Allah﴾ [ash-Shura: 10], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when others were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Grand.﴾ [Ghafir: 12], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Everything will perish except His face. For Him is the command, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [al-Qasas: 88], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for Him is the praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter; and for Him is the command, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [al-Qasas: 70], and His saying: ﴿Do they then desire the judgment of the time of ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 50], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Shall I seek other than Allah as a judge, while it is He who has sent down to you the Book, detailed?﴾ [al-An'am: 114], and to other verses besides these.

(p-259) And it is understood from these verses, such as His saying: ﴿And He does not share His command with anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 26], that those who follow the rulings of legislators other than what Allah has legislated are polytheists associating others with Allah. This understanding is explained in other verses, such as His saying concerning those who followed the Satan's legislation in permitting carrion on the claim that it is "Allah's slaughter": ﴿And do not eat from that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed it is defiantly disobedient. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you. And if you obey them, indeed you would be associators [of others with Allah].﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. So He declared them to be polytheists by their obedience. This association in obedience, and following legislation that opposes what Allah has legislated, is what is meant by the worship of Satan in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60–61], and His saying, exalted is He, concerning His prophet Ibrahim: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.﴾ [Maryam: 44], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [idols], and they invoke none but a rebellious Satan.﴾ [an-Nisa': 117]; that is, they worship none but Satan, meaning: by following his legislation. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, named those who are obeyed in what they adorn of sins "partners," in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾ to the end of the verse [al-An'am: 137]. The Prophet ﷺ explained this to 'Adi ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him, when he asked him about His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 31]; he explained to him that they made lawful for them what Allah had made unlawful and made unlawful for them what Allah had made lawful, and they followed them in that, and that this is their taking them as lords.

Among the clearest evidences for this: in Surat an-Nisa', Allah, exalted is He, explained that those who desire to submit their judgment to other than what Allah legislated are astonished at their claim of being believers; and that is only because their claim of faith together with their desire to refer judgment to the taghut is a lie so extreme that it is astonishing. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered those who claim that they have believed in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, [yet] they desire to refer [their] judgment to the taghut, although they were commanded to reject it? And Satan intends to lead them far astray.﴾ [an-Nisa': 60].

And by these divine texts that we have mentioned, it becomes utterly manifest that those who follow the man-made laws that Satan legislated through the tongues of his allies, in opposition to what Allah, exalted is He, legislated through the tongues of His messengers, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them, none doubts their disbelief and polytheism except one whose insight Allah has obliterated and whom He has blinded from the light of revelation like them.

* *

(p-260) Caution

Know that it is necessary to distinguish between a man-made system whose imposition entails disbelief in the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and a system that does not entail that.

The clarification of this: systems are of two kinds: administrative and legislative. As for the administrative, which is intended to regulate affairs and perfect them in a manner not contradicting the Sharia, there is no objection to it, and no one among the Companions, nor those after them, opposed it. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, did many things of this kind that did not exist in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, such as his recording the names of the soldiers in a register for the sake of regulation, and knowing who was absent and who was present, as we have already explained the purpose of this in Surat Bani Isra'il in the discussion of the 'aqilah who bear the blood-money for manslaughter. Although the Prophet ﷺ did not do that, and he did not know of Ka'b ibn Malik's staying behind from the Battle of Tabuk until after he had reached Tabuk ﷺ; and like 'Umar's—I mean, may Allah be pleased with him—purchase of the house of Safwan ibn Umayyah and making it a prison in Makkah the Honored, although neither the Prophet ﷺ nor Abu Bakr had taken a prison. Such administrative matters, done to perfect affairs, which do not contradict the Sharia, are not objectionable, such as organizing the affairs of employees and organizing the management of business in a manner that does not contradict the Sharia. This kind of man-made system is not objectionable, and it does not depart from the rules of the Sharia regarding consideration of public interests.

As for a legislative system that contradicts the legislation of the Creator of the heavens and the earth, its imposition is disbelief in the Creator of the heavens and the earth, such as the claim that preferring the male over the female in inheritance is not fair and that the two must be equal in inheritance; and the claim that polygamy is oppression, that divorce is oppression to the woman, and that stoning, amputation and the like are savage acts not fit to be done to a human being, and similar claims.

Therefore, the imposition of this kind of system upon the society's selves, wealth, honour, lineages, minds and religions is disbelief in the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and a rebellion against the system of Heaven, which was laid down by He who created all creatures and who knows best what benefits them, glorified and exalted is He above having any other legislator with Him, a great exaltation. ﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?﴾ [ash-Shura: 21]. ﴿Say: Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you have made from it lawful and unlawful? Say: Has Allah permitted you, or do you invent falsehood against Allah?﴾ [Yunus: 59]. ﴿And do not say, regarding what your tongues describe falsely: This is lawful and this is unlawful, to invent falsehood against Allah. Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed.﴾ [an-Nahl: 116]. We have already presented a comprehensive portion of this kind in the surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His the Exalted's words: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9], and so on.

(p-261) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, commands His Prophet ﷺ to recite this Qur'an that his Lord has revealed to him. The command in His saying "recite" (wattlu) [al-Kahf: 27] encompasses recitation in the sense of reading (al-qira'ah), and tilw in the sense of following (al-ittiba'). What this noble verse includes of His command to His Prophet ﷺ to recite the Mighty Qur'an and to follow it is clarified in other verses, such as His saying in Surat al-'Ankabut: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer﴾ and so on [al-'Ankabut: 45]; and His saying at the end of Surat al-Naml: ﴿I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred and to whom belongs everything. And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, and to recite the Qur'an﴾ and so on [al-Naml: 91-92]; ﴿And recite the Qur'an in measured recitation﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4]; and other verses that indicate the command to recite it. And His saying, commanding its following: ﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord; there is no deity except Him, and turn away from the polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 106]; His saying: ﴿So hold firmly to that which has been revealed to you; indeed, you are on a straight path﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 43]; His saying: ﴿Say, I was not something new among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am but a clear warner﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9]; and His saying: ﴿Say, it is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day﴾ [Yunus: 15]; and other verses that indicate the command to follow this Mighty Qur'an.

He has also clarified in other places some of the results that come about through reciting the Qur'an and following it, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, hope for a commerce that will never perish﴾ [Fatir: 29]; and His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recitation; those believe in it, and whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 121]. The lesson in this verse is drawn from the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion of revelation.

His saying: ﴿There is no changer of His words﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, makes clear that there is no changer of His words; that is, because its reports are true and its rulings are just, no one can change its truth into falsehood or its justice into injustice. What He mentions here is clarified in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. There is no changer of His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 115]. His saying "in truth" refers to reports, and His saying "in justice" means in rulings. And His saying: (p-262) ﴿And messengers were denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied and harmed until Our victory came to them. There is no changer of the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some of the news of the messengers﴾ [al-An'am: 34].

Allah has also clarified in other places that He changes whatever verses He wills in place of whatever verses He wills, such as His saying: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse, and Allah knows best what He sends down﴾ and so on [al-Nahl: 101]; His saying: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth one better than it or similar to it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106]; and His saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord"﴾ [Yunus: 15]. (Note: this last citation as given in the source is al-Kahf: 27, and the translation above follows the source's reference text.)

His saying: ﴿And you will not find other than Him any refuge﴾.

The origin of al-multahad (refuge) is the place of inclination (multahad, from al-ilhad, the form ilti-hād), from al-lahd meaning inclination; from it comes al-lahd in the grave, because it is an inclination in the digging. From it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses are not hidden from Us﴾ [Fussilat: 40], and His saying: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾ and so on [al-A'raf: 180]. So the meaning of lahd and ilhad in this is inclination away from the truth, and the mulhid is one who inclines away from the religion of truth. It is established in the science of morphology (al-sarf) that if the past tense of a verb exceeds three letters, its mimi verbal noun, its noun of place and its noun of time are all in the form of the passive participle, as here. So al-multahad is in the form of the passive participle, and what is meant by it is the place of refuge, that is, the place to which one inclines seeking a shelter or a refuge that saves him from what Allah wills to do to him.

What He mentions here, that His Prophet ﷺ does not find other than Him any multahad, that is, a place to which he inclines and takes refuge if he does not convey the message of his Lord and obey Him, is clarified in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Say, "I possess not for you any harm or right guidance." Say, "Indeed, no one will protect me from Allah, nor will I find other than Him any refuge, but [I convey] from Allah and His messages"﴾ [al-Jinn: 21-22]; and His saying: ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some [of His] sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand and then cut from him the aorta, and not one of you could have prevented Us from him﴾ and so on [al-Haqqah: 44-47].

That he has no multahad, that is, a place to which he takes refuge, has a counterpart in the Qur'an expressed in different wordings, such as al-manas, al-mahis, al-malja', al-mawil, al-mafarr and al-wazar: His saying: ﴿Then they called out, but it was no time for escape﴾ [Sad: 3]; His saying: ﴿And they will not find from it any escape﴾ [al-Nisa': 121]; His saying: ﴿So they roamed through the lands; is there any escape?﴾ [Qaf: 36]; His saying: ﴿You will have no refuge that Day, nor will you have any denial﴾ [al-Shura: 47]; His saying: ﴿Rather, for them is a promise; they will not find other than Him any refuge﴾ [al-Kahf: 58]; (p-263) and His saying: ﴿The human being will say on that Day, "Where is the escape?" No! There is no refuge﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 10-11]. All of these refer in meaning to one thing: the absence of a place to which they can turn and in which they can take shelter.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 28:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to make himself patient, that is, to restrain himself along with the believers who call upon their Lord at the beginning and end of the day, sincere to Him, seeking by their supplication nothing but His pleasure, Mighty and Majestic.

This noble verse was revealed concerning the poor emigrants, such as 'Ammar, Suhayb, Bilal, Ibn Mas'ud and others like them, when the chieftains of the disbelievers wanted the Prophet ﷺ to drive them away from him and to sit with him without the presence of those poor believers. We have already mentioned in surah al-An'am that Allah, just as He commanded him here to keep himself patient with them, commanded him not to drive them away, and that when he saw them he should greet them with peace. This is in His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. You are not accountable for their account at all, nor are they accountable for yours at all, so that you would drive them away and thus be among the wrongdoers﴾ – up to His saying – ﴿And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say: Peace be upon you﴾ [al-An'am: 52–54]. He also alluded to this meaning in His saying: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded and the reminder would benefit him. As for him who considers himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention. Yet it is not your responsibility if he does not purify himself. But as for him who came to you hastening, fearing [Allah], from him you are distracted. No! [Indeed it is a reminder]﴾ [‘Abasa: 1–11]. We have also mentioned that what the disbelievers asked of our Prophet ﷺ, namely to drive away the poor and weak believers, out of arrogance toward them and contempt for them, was also asked of Noah by the people of Noah, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, and that he likewise refused to drive them away. Allah says of them: ﴿They said: Shall we believe you, when the lowest people follow you?﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 111]. And they also said: ﴿And we do not see anyone following you except those who are the lowest of us, without considered judgment﴾ [Hud: 27]. And of Noah, regarding his refusal to drive them away, He said: ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers. I am only a clear warner﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 114]. And as He said of him: ﴿And I will not drive away those who believe. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are ignorant. And O my people, who would protect me from Allah if I drove them away? Will you not remember?﴾ [Hud: 29–30].

As for His saying: ﴿And keep yourself patient﴾ [al-Kahf: 28], in it is evidence that the root ṣabara (to be patient) is transitive by itself to its object, and a parallel to this in the speech of the Arabs is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb or 'Antarah:

"So she endured, knowing this, a free woman who stands firm when the soul of the coward rises in alarm."

Al-ghadah means the beginning of the day, and al-'ashiyy means its end. Some scholars said: ﴿calling upon their Lord morning and evening﴾ means they pray the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. But the accurate view is that the verse includes something more general than merely the prayer, and Allah knows best.

* *

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade His Prophet ﷺ from letting his eyes stray away from the weak believers and their poor, out of longing for the rich and what they possess of the adornment of the worldly life. The meaning of ﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them﴾ [al-Kahf: 28] is: do not let your eyes go beyond them and turn away from the shabbiness of their dress, looking down on them and aspiring to the people of wealth, status and nobility in their place. ‘Adā ya'dū means: it is transitive by itself to the object, and it is also intransitive. The clause in His saying: ﴿desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾ is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and the linking element is the pronoun, according to the rule in His saying in al-Khulasa (Ibn Malik's Alfiyya on Arabic grammar):

"And a clause that begins with a present-tense verb that is established, containing a pronoun, and free of the waw."

The one whose state is described is the pronoun attached to the noun in His saying "your eyes" (ʿaynāka). This was permissible because the noun here is a part of the noun to which it is attached, according to the rule in al-Khulasa:

"Do not permit a circumstantial clause from the genitive noun, except when the genitive noun requires its governance, or when it is a part of what belongs to it, or like its part; then do not err."

What Allah forbade His Prophet ﷺ from in this noble verse is the eye's aspiring to the adornment of the worldly life, while he is characterized by what pleases Him, Mighty and Majestic, namely steadfastness upon the truth, such as sitting with the poor believers. He also alluded to this in other places, such as His saying: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased. And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to categories of them, the splendor of the worldly life﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130–131]; and His saying: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the often-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an. Do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to categories of them﴾ – the verse – [al-Hijr: 87].

* *

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade His Prophet ﷺ from obeying one whose heart Allah has made heedless of His remembrance, who follows his desire, and whose affair is fruṭan (in neglect). He has repeated in the Qur'an the prohibition to His Prophet ﷺ against following such a person who is heedless of the remembrance of Allah and follows his desire, as in His saying: ﴿So be patient for the decision of your Lord and do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ [al-Insan: 24]; and His saying: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and leave off their harm﴾ – the verse – [al-Ahzab: 48]; (p. 265) and His saying: ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise. And do not obey every habitual swearer, contemptible, going around with slander, hindering the good, transgressing, sinful, rough and additionally of illegitimate birth﴾ [al-Qalam: 8–12], and other verses besides these.

He also commanded him in another place to turn away from those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah and who desire nothing but the worldly life, and He made clear to him that this is the extent of their knowledge. That is in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So turn away from one who turns away from Our remembrance and desires nothing but the worldly life. That is the extent of their knowledge﴾.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿whose heart We have made heedless﴾ [al-Kahf: 28] indicates that what befalls the servant of heedlessness and disobedience is only by the will of Allah, the Exalted, since nothing whatsoever occurs, whatever it may be, except by His universal, decreed will, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ – the verse – [al-Insan: 30]; ﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 107]; ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [as-Sajdah: 13]; ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 35]; ﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts﴾ – the verse – [al-Baqarah: 7]; ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-Isra': 46]; and other verses that indicate that everything, good or evil, occurs only by the will of the Creator of the heavens and the earth. What the Mu'tazilah claim, and what al-Zamakhshari always attempts in his tafsir, namely interpreting the verses of the Qur'an in a way that agrees with the independence of the servant's power and will, so that his actions are apart from the will of Allah, is manifestly false, as the verses mentioned above indicate, and similar verses in the Qur'an are numerous.

The meaning of his following his desire is that he follows what his commanding soul inclines toward and desires of evil, such as disbelief and sins.

His saying: ﴿and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾ – it has been said that this is from tafrīṭ (neglect), which is shortcoming, and the preceding of helplessness by abandoning faith. On this view, the meaning of ﴿and whose affair has been [ever] in neglect﴾ is: his deeds were folly, loss and negligence. It has also been said that it is from ifrāṭ (excess), which is transgressing the limit, like the saying of the disbelievers who looked down on the poor believers: "We are the nobles of Mudar and its leaders! If we follow you, all the people will follow you." This is from arrogance and excess in speech. It has also been said that "furuṭan" means: formerly in evil, from their saying: "such-and-such a matter preceded from him," meaning it went before. The most apparent of the views on the meaning of this noble verse, in my opinion, according to the Arabic language in which the Qur'an was revealed, is that the meaning of His saying "furuṭan" is: going before the truth and the right, casting it behind his back. From their saying: "a furus horse," meaning one that goes ahead of the horses; and from this is the saying of Labid in his Mu'allaqah:

"I have protected the horses, bearing my armour; the thread of my sword-belt goes ahead when I set out to their bridles."

All the views of the commentators go back to what we have mentioned about the meaning of the verse. Such as the saying of Qatadah and Mujahid, "furuṭan" means: loss. And the saying of Muqatil ibn Hayyan, "furuṭan" means: extravagance. And the saying of al-Farra', "furuṭan" means: abandoned. And the saying of al-Akhfash, "furuṭan" means: exceeding the limit, and other views besides these.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted and majestic is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to say to the people: "The truth is from your Lord." Regarding its i'rab (grammatical analysis), there are two possibilities. The first is that "al-haqq" (the truth) is a mubtada' (nominal subject), and the prepositional phrase "from your Lord" is its khabar (predicate). The meaning is: the truth that I have brought you in this magnificent Qur'an, which includes the religion of Islam, has its origin from your Lord, exalted is He. Therefore, it is not from the inspiration of Satan, nor from the fabrications of soothsayers, nor from the myths of the ancients, nor anything else. Rather, it is from your Creator, exalted is He, whose obedience and monotheism are obligatory upon you. Nothing comes from Him except the truth, which encompasses truthfulness in reports and justice in rulings. There is no truth except from Him, exalted is He.

The second possibility is that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtada', meaning: "This which I have brought you is the truth."

What Allah mentioned in this noble verse, He also mentioned in other places, such as His saying in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [al-Baqarah: 147], and His saying in Al 'Imran: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Al 'Imran: 60], and other verses.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾. The apparent meaning of this noble verse, according to the linguistic convention, is giving choice between disbelief and belief. However, the intended meaning of the verse is not choice; rather, what is intended is threat and warning. Threatening with a form whose apparent meaning is choice is one of the styles of the Arabic language. The evidence from the Mighty Qur'an that the intended meaning in the verse is threat and warning is that He followed it with His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will enclose them. And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like murky oil that scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place﴾. This is the clearest evidence that the intended meaning is threat and warning, for if choice were on its own basis, He would not have threatened the one who chooses either of the two options with this painful punishment. This is clear, as you see.

His saying in this noble verse, a'tadna [﴿We have prepared﴾] [al-Kahf: 29], its root is from al-i'tad, and the taa' in it is original, not substituted from a dal, according to the more correct view. From it comes al-'atad, meaning readiness for something. The meaning of "a'tadna" is: We have lain in wait and prepared. By "the wrongdoers" here is meant: the disbelievers, as evidenced by His saying before it: ﴿And whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾. We have previously mentioned how frequently wrongdoing (zulm) is used for disbelief in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13], His saying: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254], and His saying: ﴿And do not invoke other than Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you; for if you did, you would then be among the wrongdoers﴾ [Yunus: 106], and similar verses.

We have previously stated that zulm in the language of the Arabs is placing a thing in other than its proper place. Among the greatest of this is placing worship upon a created being. The Qur'an also uses zulm for deficiency, in His saying: ﴿and did not fall short of it in anything﴾ [al-Kahf: 33]. The root meaning of the word zulm is what we have mentioned, placing a thing other than its proper place. For this reason, it is said of one who strikes the milk before it has churned that he is a zalim (wrongdoer), because he has placed the striking of his milk in other than its proper place; for striking it before it churns wastes its butter. From this meaning is the saying of the poet:
