"They go down into Najd and into a deep low ground, deviating (fawasiqan) from their intended course, straying (jawa'iran)."

This meaning is apparent and there is no difficulty in it, so there is no need for the saying of one who said that "ʿan" (عن) here is causal, as in His saying: ﴿And we will not leave our gods on account of your word﴾ [Hud 11:53], meaning: because of it; and that the meaning is "he defied on account of the command of his Lord," i.e., because of His command, in that he did not comply with it; nor for any other of the sayings.

His saying in this noble verse, ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me, while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾, the hamzah (أ) here is for denunciation and rebuke, and there is no doubt that it carries the sense of astonishment (istib'ad), as its counterpart has been mentioned many times before. That is: how far is what has appeared from him of defiance and disobedience, and the intensity of his enmity toward you and toward your two parents, Adam and Hawwa', from taking him and his offspring as allies in place of your Creator, majestic and exalted! "Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers": the exchange from God is Iblis and his offspring. "For the wrongdoers" means: because they took falsehood in exchange for truth and put their allegiance to Iblis and his offspring in place of their allegiance to God. This is among the most grievous forms of wrongdoing, which in the language means placing a thing in other than its proper place, as has been mentioned many times before. The one singled out for blame in the verse is omitted, and the context indicates it; its estimated form is: "Wretched is the exchange from God: Iblis and his offspring." The subject of "wretched" (bi'sa) is an omitted pronoun explained by the tamyiz (specification) which is "badalan" (exchange), in accordance with his saying in the Khulasah:

"And two elevate a hidden pronoun which the specifier explains, as in 'how excellent is a people, their group.'"

Al-badal means the substitute for a thing. What He, majestic and exalted, mentioned in this noble verse about the enmity of Satan toward the children of Adam has been made clear in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ [Fatir 35:6]. Likewise the two parents, as He said: ﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not drive you both out of Paradise and [thus] you become distressed"﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:117].

He has made clear in another place that those who took the devils as allies in place of God's allegiance think that they are in the right, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies besides God, and they think that they are guided﴾ [al-A'raf 7:30]. And He has made clear in other places that the disbelievers are allies of Satan, as in His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut, so fight against the allies of Satan﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:76]; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾ [al-A'raf 7:27]; and His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve, their allies are the Taghut﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:257]; and His saying: ﴿That is only Satan frightening you of his allies, so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:175], and other verses.

His saying in this noble verse, "and his offspring" [al-Kahf 18:50], is evidence that Satan has offspring. So the claim that he has no offspring contradicts this verse in an explicit contradiction, as you see. And whatever explicitly contradicts the clear text of the Qur'an is false beyond doubt! However, the manner in which his progeny come into existence, whether by marriage or otherwise, has no proof from an explicit text, and scholars differ concerning it. Al-Sha'bi said: "A man asked me: Does Iblis have a wife? I said: That is a wedding I did not witness." Then I recalled His saying: ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me?﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50], so I knew that there can be no offspring except from a wife, and I said: "Yes." What al-Sha'bi understood from this verse, that offspring entails a wife, was also related similarly from Qatadah. Mujahid said: The manner in which offspring comes from him is that he inserted his private part into his own private part, and he laid five eggs. He said: "This is the origin of his offspring." Some people of knowledge said: God created for him in his right thigh a male organ and in his left a female organ, so he couples this with that, and there comes forth for him every day ten eggs, from each egg there emerges seventy devils, male and female. It is not hidden that these sayings and the like have no reliance placed upon them, for they are not supported by evidence from the Book or the Sunnah. The noble verse indicates that he has offspring. As for the manner of the birth of that offspring, no sound transmission has been established concerning it, and such matters cannot be known by opinion. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this verse: "I say: what has been established in this subject from the sound reports is what al-Himyari mentioned in al-Jam' bayn al-Sahihayn from Imam Abu Bakr al-Barqani: that he transmitted in his book, with a chain, from Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id the memorizer, from the narration of 'Asim, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'Do not be the first to enter the marketplace, nor the last to leave it, for in it Satan lays eggs and hatches.'" This indicates that Satan has offspring from his loins.

The author, may Allah pardon him, said: This hadith only indicates that he lays eggs and hatches them, but there is no indication in it as to whether these are from a female who is his wife or from something else. Moreover, the indication of the hadith to what we have mentioned is not free from possibility, because it is common in the speech of the Arabs to use "he laid eggs" and "he hatched" as a figure of speech (mathal). So the meaning of "he laid eggs and hatched" may be that he does with them whatever he wishes of misguidance, seduction, whispering and the like, as a figure of speech, since proverbs do not have their wording changed. As for what many exegetes (mufassirun) and others mention, specifying the names of his children and the functions he assigned to them, such as "Zalanbur, lord of the markets," and "Tibr, lord of calamities, who orders the striking of faces, the tearing of collars and the like," and "al-A'war, lord of the gates of adultery," and "Miswat, lord of news, who casts it into the mouths of people so that they find no basis for it," and "Dasim, who is the devil that, when a man enters his house without greeting and without mentioning the name of Allah, causes him to see what is not to be taken up and what is not placed in its right place, and stirs up evil against his family; and when he eats without mentioning the name of Allah, he eats with him," and "al-Wahlan, lord of the flutes, after whom Iblis was known by kunya," and beyond that of specifying their names and functions, all of it is not to be relied upon, except what has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ). Among what has been established from him (ﷺ) concerning the specifying of the devil's function and name is what Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated in his Sahih (authentic collection): Yahya ibn Khalaf al-Bahili narrated to us, Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Juraayri, from Abu al-Ala': that Uthman ibn Abi al-As came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed the devil has come between me and my prayer and my recitation; he confuses it for me!" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is a devil called Khinzab. When you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him, and spit to your left three times." He said: "So I did that, and Allah removed him from me."

And the inciting of discord among people by the devil, and that Iblis places his throne upon the sea and sends out his battalions, so that they tempt people, and the greatest of them in his sight is the greatest in temptation, all of this is well known and established in the Sahih. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 51:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misguiders as helpers (ʿadud)﴾. The verified meaning of this noble verse is that Allah says: I did not make Iblis and his hosts witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, so that I might seek their help in creating them, nor [did I make them witness] the creation of themselves; that is, I did not make some of them witness the creation of others so that I might seek help from them in creating Him. Rather, I alone created all of that, without any helper or supporter! So how can you give them My right and take them as allies besides Me, when I am the Creator of everything?

This meaning which the verse points to, namely that the Creator is the One and only deity worthy of worship, is clarified in many verses, and we have already cited many of them in various places, such as His saying: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not remember?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17]; His saying: ﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of everything, and He is the One, the Subduer﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16]; His saying: ﴿This is the creation of Allah; so show me what those besides Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in manifest error﴾ [Luqman: 11]; His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ [Fatir: 40]; and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 4], along with other verses besides these, as we have mentioned repeatedly. Some scholars said: ﴿nor the creation of themselves﴾ means: I did not make them witness the creation of themselves; rather, I created them as I willed and in the manner I chose.

His saying, Exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿nor was I one to take misguiders as helpers (ʿadud)﴾ [al-Kahf: 51]. Here there is the use of an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, since the original form would be the pronoun: "nor was I one to take them as helpers," like His saying: ﴿I did not make them witness﴾. The rhetorical purpose of using the explicit noun in place of the pronoun is to censure them by the word (p-295) "misguiders." And His saying "ʿadud" means: helpers.

In this noble verse there is an admonition that it is not fitting to seek help from those who are astray and who lead others astray; and the lesson is drawn from the generality of the wording, not from the specific occasion of revelation.

The meaning mentioned here is also pointed to in other places, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He said: My Lord, because You have bestowed favor upon me, I will never be a supporter (ẓahīr) of the criminals﴾ [al-Qasas: 17]. The ẓahīr is the helper, and the misguiders are those who lead their followers away from the path of truth. We have already presented the meaning of error (ḍalāl) and its usages in the Qur'an with their Arabic evidences.

The Qur'anic text: "And [mention] the Day when He will say, 'Call upon My partners whom you claimed,' so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them; and We will place between them a barrier of destruction" (Q. 18:52).

That is, mention the Day when Allah, exalted and majestic is He, says to the polytheists who used to associate with Him gods and equals from among idols and other objects of worship besides Allah, rebuking and reproaching them: "Call upon My partners whom you claimed," meaning that they were partners with Me. The two objects are omitted: the meaning is "whom you claimed to be partners for Me, falsely and fabrications." That is, call upon them and seek their aid, that they may help you and protect you from My punishment. "So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them," that is, they will seek their help, but they will not help them.

What Allah, exalted is He, mentions in this noble verse, namely that they will not respond to them when they call upon them on the Day of Resurrection, is made clear in other passages, such as His saying in Surat al-Qasas: "And [mention] the Day when He will call to them and say, 'Where are My partners whom you used to claim?'" "Those upon whom the word has come into effect will say, 'Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray; we led them astray as we ourselves were astray. We disassociate ourselves before You. They did not used to worship us.'" "And it will be said, 'Call upon your partners.' So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided!" [Q. 28:62–64]. And His saying: "That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you call upon besides Him do not possess [even] a thin membrane of a date seed. If you call upon them, they do not hear your call, and even if they heard, they could not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association [of them with Allah]. And none can inform you like the Acquainted [Allah]" [Q. 35:13–14]. And His saying: "And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship" [Q. 46:5–6]. And His saying: "And they have taken besides Allah gods that they might be for them a source of honor. No! They will deny their worship of them and will become opponents to them" [Q. 19:81–82]. And His saying, exalted is He: "And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We bestowed upon you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners [of Allah] among you. The connections between you have been cut off, and lost from you is what you used to claim" [Q. 6:94]. The verses about their disavowal of them on the Day of Resurrection, and their not responding to them, are very numerous.

The sermon of Satan mentioned in Surat Ibrahim, at [p. 296] His saying: "And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, 'Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you…'" up to His saying: "Indeed, I have disbelieved in your associating me [with Allah] before" [Q. 14:22], is of the same kind as the meaning mentioned in the aforementioned verses.

As for His saying in this noble verse, "And We will place between them a barrier of destruction," the scholars differed concerning it from three aspects:

The first: concerning the intended meaning of the adverbial expression, which is "bayn" (between). The second: concerning the referent of the pronoun. The third: concerning the intended meaning of "mawbiq" (barrier of destruction).

We will mention here their opinions and what appears to us to be the most correct of them, if Allah the Exalted wills.

As for "mawbiq": it was said to mean "the destroyer." It was also said to be a valley in Hell. It was also said to be "the appointed place." The author of ad-Durr al-Manthur said: Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through the chain of 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, "And We will place between them a barrier of destruction," that he said: "a destroyer." Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying "mawbiq," that he said: "a destroyer." Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid, concerning His saying "mawbiq," that he said: "a valley in Hell."

'Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in Zawa'id az-Zuhd, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in ash-Shu'ab, from Anas, concerning His saying: "And We will place between them a barrier of destruction," that he said: "A valley in Hell of pus and blood." Ahmad in az-Zuhd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Umar, concerning His saying: "And We will place between them a barrier of destruction," that he said: "It is a deep valley in the Fire, by which Allah will separate, on the Day of Resurrection, between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance." Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Amr al-Bikali, who said: "The mawbiq that Allah mentioned is a valley in the Fire, of great depth, by which Allah will separate, on the Day of Resurrection, between the people of Islam and all others among mankind." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ikrimah concerning His saying, exalted is He, "mawbiq," that he said: "It is a river flowing with fire, on whose banks are serpents like dark mules; when they rise up against them to seize them, they seek refuge by plunging into the Fire from it." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ka'b, who said: "In the Fire there are four valleys with which Allah punishes its people: Ghalith, Mawbiq, Athham, and Ghayy." End of the words of the author of ad-Durr al-Manthur.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from some of the people of knowledge of Arabic language among the people of Basra that "mawbiq" means "appointed place," and he cited as evidence the verse of the poet:

"And Sharwarā and as-Sitār have bestowed [rain] so that it left no trace of ... for it, and the two valleys at a mawbiq."

That is, at an appointed place. The verified position is that mawbiq means "the destroyer," from their saying "wabaqa yabiqu," like "wa'ada ya'idu," meaning "he perished," (p-297) when he perished. There is another dialect for it, which is "wabaqa yaubaqu," like "wajila yaujalu." And a third dialect as well, which is "wabaqa yabiqu," like "waritha yaritha." The meaning of all of them is destruction. The verbal noun of "wabaqa" with fatha is al-wubuq, by analogy, and al-wabq. And from "wabaqa" with kasra is al-wabaq with two fathas, by analogy. "His sins caused him to perish" (awbaqathu dhunubuhu): they destroyed him. From this meaning is His saying, exalted is He: "Or He may cause them to perish for what they have earned" [Q. 42:34], that is, destroy them. From it is the hadith: "Whoever sells himself, destroys himself (fa-mūbiqun nafsahu), or frees it" and the hadith "the seven destroying sins (al-mūbiqāt)," that is, the destructive ones. From this meaning is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And whoever buys good repute with his wealth, will guard his honor from every shameful, destroying thing."

As for the saying of one who said that mawbiq is enmity, and the saying of one who said it is the assembly, both are clearly weak. The verified position regarding it is what we have presented. As for the opinions of the scholars concerning the intended meaning of the word "bayn" (between): according to the view of al-Hasan and those who agree with him, that mawbiq is enmity, the meaning is clear; that is, "And We placed between them enmity," like His saying: "The close friends that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous" [Q. 43:67], and His saying: "And he said, 'You have taken only idols besides Allah as a bond of affection among yourselves in the worldly life; then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and some of you will curse others'" [Q. 29:25], and other verses. But interpreting mawbiq as enmity is far-fetched, as we have mentioned. Some scholars said: the intended meaning of "bayn" (between) in the verse is "connection"; that is, "And We made their mutual connections in the world a possession for them on the Day of Resurrection," as Allah, exalted is He, said: "When those who were followed will disassociate themselves from those who followed, and they will see the punishment, and their bonds will be cut off" [Q. 2:166], that is, the connections that were between them in the world. And as He said: "No! They will deny their worship of them and will become opponents to them" [Q. 19:82], and as He, exalted is He, said: "Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and some of you will curse others" [Q. 29:25], and similar verses. Some scholars said: "And We placed between them a barrier of destruction" means: We placed destruction between them, because each of them helps in the destruction of the other, through their cooperation in disbelief and sins; so they are partners in the punishment, as Allah, exalted is He, said: "And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you will be sharers in the punishment" [Q. 43:39], and His saying: "He will say, 'For each is double, but you do not know'" [Q. 7:38]. The meaning of this view is narrated from Ibn Zayd. Some scholars said: "And We placed between them a barrier of destruction" means: between the believers and the disbelievers a barrier of destruction, that is, a destroyer that separates them; so whoever enters it is in destruction, and whoever is outside it is in well-being. The most apparent of the views to me, and the one most consistent with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, is that the meaning is: "And We placed between the disbelievers and those whom they used to worship and associate with Allah a barrier of destruction, that is, a destroyer" (p-298) because all of them are encompassed by destruction from every side, as Allah, exalted is He, said: "They will have above them layers of Fire and below them layers" [Q. 39:16], and His saying: "They will have from Hell a bed and over them coverings" [Q. 7:41], and His saying: "Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the firewood of Hell" [Q. 21:98], and the verse. Ibn al-A'rabi said: "Everything that is a barrier between two things is called mawbiq," which al-Qurtubi transmitted from him. From what we have mentioned, you will know that the pronoun in His saying "baynahum" (between them) is said to refer to the people of the Fire. It is also said to refer to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire together. And it is said to refer to the polytheists and what they used to worship besides Allah. This last is the most apparent of them, because of the indication of the apparent context: since Allah says, "And [mention] the Day when He will say, 'Call upon My partners whom you claimed,' so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them" [Q. 18:52], then He said, informing about the worshippers and the worshipped: "And We placed between them a barrier of destruction" [Q. 18:52], that is, a destroyer that separates them and encompasses them. This meaning is like His saying: "And [mention] the Day when We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated [others with Allah], 'Remain in your place, you and your partners.' Then We will separate them" [Q. 10:28], that is, We will separate them.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse, "wa-yawma yaqūlu" (and the Day when He says): the majority of the seven readers, except Hamzah, read it with the yā' (third person), while Hamzah read "naqūlu" with the nūn of majesty. According to the reading of the majority, the subject is a pronoun referring to Allah, that is, He says, that is, Allah.

The Exalted said: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire, and they will think that they are about to fall into it, and they will not find any way of escape from it.﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted mentions that the criminals will see the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and will think that they are about to plunge into it, meaning that they will mix with it and fall into it. Here *al-zann* (supposition) carries the meaning of *al-yaqin* (certainty), because they will have witnessed the realities and beheld what is actually happening. The Exalted has made clear in other places that they will be certain of the reality, as in His saying about them: ﴿If you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back; we will act righteously; indeed, we are certain."﴾ [As-Sajdah: 12]; and His saying: ﴿So We have removed from you your covering, and so your sight today is sharp.﴾ [Qaf: 22]; and His saying: ﴿How clearly they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us!﴾ [Maryam: 38]. Among the uses of *al-zann* for *al-yaqin* is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humble, who are certain [*yazunnuna*] that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 45–46], meaning: they are certain that they will meet their Lord. And His saying: ﴿Those who are certain [*yazunnuna*] that they will meet Allah said, "How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah! And Allah is with the patient."﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 249]; and His saying: ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain [*zanantu*] that I would meet my account."﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 19–20]. So *al-zann* in all these verses means *al-yaqin*. The Arabs use *al-zann* for both certainty and doubt. Among its uses for certainty in Arabic speech is the verse of Durayd ibn al-Simmah:

*So I said to them: "Be certain (of) two thousand armored men, their chiefs in the Persian coats of mail."*

And the verse of Umayrah ibn Tariq:

*That you raid my people while I remain among you, and I make of my supposition an unseen target, hurled.*

The Exalted has also mentioned in this noble verse that the criminals see the Fire, and He has made clear in another place that it also sees them, as in His saying: ﴿Rather, they denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blaze. When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring.﴾ [Al-Furqan: 11–12]. As for what is common on the tongues of scholars, that *al-zann* is the general category of *i'tiqad* (belief), this is a technical convention of the scholars of legal theory (*usuliyyun*) and the jurists (*fuqaha'*), and there is no dispute over a convention.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and they will not find any way of escape from it﴾, *al-masrif* means *al-ma'dil* (the place of turning away or deviation), meaning: they will not find from the Fire any place to turn to and deviate to, to take as a refuge and a stronghold by which they may be saved from the punishment of Allah. Among the uses of *al-masrif* in the sense of *al-ma'dil*, meaning a place of turning to seek protection in that place, is the saying of Abu Kabir al-Hudhali:

*O Zuhayr, is there no way of escape for Shaybah? Or is there no eternity for one who gives generously and strives?*

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire﴾, *ra'a* here is the visual sense (*al-basariyyah*), so it takes one object. The expression of the past tense for the future is because its occurrence is certain, so this is as though its occurrence were already happening, as has been mentioned many times before. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

[p. 300] His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people from every kind of example, but man has been most contentious of things﴾ [al-Kahf 18:54]. His saying, ﴿And We have certainly diversified﴾, means: We repeated and multiplied the diversification of examples (amthal), with varied expressions and diverse methods, in this Qur'an for the people, so that they might be guided to the truth and be admonished. But they opposed it with contention and dispute. A mathal (example, parable) is a strange saying that travels throughout the horizons. The coining of examples is very frequent in the Qur'an, as Exalted is He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:26]. Among the examples coined in it is ﴿O people, an example has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will not create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj 22:73]. And His saying: ﴿The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which takes a home; and indeed, the frailest of homes is the spider's home, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:41]. [p. 300] And His saying: ﴿So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will reflect﴾ ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf 7:176-177]. And like His saying: ﴿The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not carry it is like the example of a donkey carrying books. Evil is the example of the people who denied the signs of Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 62:5]. And His saying: ﴿And present to them the example of the life of this world: it is like water which We sent down from the sky﴾ [al-Kahf 18:45]. And His saying: ﴿Allah presents an example: a slave owned, having no power over anything, and one We had provided with good provision from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise be to Allah; but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Nahl 16:75]. And His saying: ﴿And Allah presents an example: two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, and he is a burden upon his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path?﴾ [al-Nahl 16:76]. And His saying: ﴿He presents to you an example from yourselves: do you have among what your right hands possess partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear one another?﴾ [al-Rum 30:28]. The verses of this kind are very numerous. In these examples and their likes in the Qur'an are very great lessons, admonitions and deterrents, with no ambiguity about the truth accompanying them; however, only the people of knowledge understand their meanings, as Exalted is He said: ﴿And these examples We present to the people, but none understands them except the knowledgeable﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:43]. Among the wisdoms of coining examples is that people may remember, as Exalted is He said: ﴿And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought﴾ [al-Hashr 59:21].

Exalted is He has explained in other places that examples, along with their clarification of the truth, by which Allah guides a people and misleads other people, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it. As for those who believed, they know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieved, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads thereby many and guides thereby many, and He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:26]. He alluded to this meaning in Surat al-Ra'd, because when He coined the example with His saying: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their measure, and the flood carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire seeking ornament or goods is a foam like it. Thus Allah presents the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but that which benefits the people remains upon the earth. Thus Allah presents examples﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:17], He followed that with His saying: ﴿For those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]; but those who did not respond to Him — if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves by it. For them is an evil account, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:18]. There is no doubt that those who [p. 301] responded to their Lord are the intelligent ones who understood the meaning of the examples and benefited from what they contained of the clarification of the truth, and that those who did not respond to Him are those who did not understand them and did not recognise the realities they made clear. So the first group is the one of whom Allah said, ﴿and He guides thereby many﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:26], and the second group is the one of whom He said, ﴿He misleads thereby many﴾, and of whom He said, ﴿and He misleads thereby none but the defiantly disobedient﴾.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿And We have certainly diversified﴾, some scholars said: the object of "ṣarrafnā" (We diversified) is omitted; its estimate is: "the clear signs (al-bayyināt) and lessons (al-ʿibar)". On this basis, "min" (from) indicates the starting point of the extent, meaning: And We certainly diversified the signs and lessons, from the kinds of coining examples, for the people in this Qur'an, so that they might be reminded. They met that with argument and disputation, and therefore He said: ﴿but man has been most contentious of things﴾ [al-Kahf 18:54]. This is what Abu Hayyan preferred in al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit). Then he said: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "min" may be extra (zā'ida) for emphasis, so the estimate is: "And We certainly diversified every example", and the object of "ṣarrafnā" would then be "kull mathal" (every example). This parsing is according to the school of the Kufans and al-Akhfash, not according to the view of the majority of the Basrans. The purpose of the speech of the author of al-Bahr al-Muhit ends. Al-Zamakhshari said: "min kulli mathal" means: from every meaning which is like the example in its strangeness and its beauty. End of quotation. The rule of coining an example, to which all the meanings by which it is explained return, is: clarifying the meaning of a counterpart by mentioning its counterpart, because the counterpart is known by its counterpart. This meaning mentioned in this noble verse is also stated in other verses, such as His saying in al-Isra': ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example, but most of the people refused except disbelief﴾ [al-Isra' 17:89], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an that they may be reminded, but it increases them only in aversion﴾ [al-Isra' 17:41], and His saying: ﴿And thus We revealed it as an Arabic Qur'an and diversified in it of the warning that perhaps they will fear Allah or it will produce for them remembrance﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:113], and His saying: ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every example that perhaps they will remember﴾ ﴿An Arabic Qur'an without any crookedness that perhaps they will fear Allah﴾ [al-Zumar 39:27-28], and His saying: ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every example, but if you brought them a sign, those who disbelieved would surely say, "You are not but falsifiers"﴾ [al-Rum 30:58]. The verses of this kind are very numerous.

As for His saying in this verse: ﴿but man has been most contentious of things﴾ [al-Kahf 18:54]: that is, the most of the things that are apt to produce contention, if you explain them one by one, "jadalan" means: contention and disputation with falsehood, for the purpose of refuting the truth.

Among the verses indicating that man contends with falsehood to refute the truth is His saying here: ﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood to refute thereby the truth﴾ [al-Kahf 18:56], [p. 302] and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who argue about Allah after it has been responded to, their argument is invalid with their Lord﴾ [al-Shura 42:16], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Does man not see that We created him from a sperm drop, and then he is an open adversary?﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:77], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He created man from a sperm drop, and then he is an open adversary﴾ [al-Nahl 16:4], and others besides these verses.

What we explained His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿but man has been most contentious of things﴾ to mean that its meaning is the abundance of the disbelievers' contention and disputation with falsehood, to refute the truth thereby, is the context in which this noble verse was revealed. For His saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example﴾ [al-Isra' 17:89], meaning: that they may be reminded, admonished and turn back to their Lord, is evidenced by His saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an that they may be reminded﴾ [al-Isra' 17:41], and His saying: ﴿And this is how We present the examples to the people that perhaps they will reflect﴾ [al-Hashr 59:21]. Since He followed that with His saying: ﴿but man has been most contentious of things﴾, we know from the context of the verse that the disbelievers multiplied contention, dispute and argument to refute the truth which Allah made clear by what He coined in this Qur'an of every example. But that this is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) does not contradict interpreting the noble verse by the apparent generality of its wording, because the consideration is for the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion, as we demonstrated with its proofs earlier. For this reason, when "the Prophet ﷺ knocked on ʿAlī and Fāṭima (may Allah be pleased with them both) one night and said: 'Will you not pray?' ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in the hand of Allah; if He wills to raise us, He raises us.' The Prophet ﷺ turned back, striking his thigh and saying: '[And man has been most contentious of things]'." The hadith is well known and agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh). His ﷺ citing of the verse in response to ʿAlī's (may Allah be pleased with him) saying, "our souls are in the hand of Allah; if He wills to raise us, He raises us," is evidence for the generality of the noble verse and its inclusion of every dispute and contention. However, other verses indicate that among contention there is what is praiseworthy and commanded for the manifestation of the truth, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And argue with them in a way that is best﴾ [al-Nahl 16:125], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:46].

His saying "jadalan" is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz), according to the rule of his saying in the Khulasa (Ibn Malik's Alfiyya):

"And the agent of meaning in the elative, put in the accusative: like 'you are highest in station'."

His saying: ﴿most contentious of things﴾ means: the most of the things from which contention can arise, in contention, as preceded. The elative form (ṣīghat al-tafḍīl), when it is annexed to an indefinite noun, as in this verse, or stripped of annexation and of definition by "al-", it must be kept singular and masculine, as he set out in the Khulasa with his saying:

"And if it is attached to an indefinite, or stripped, bind it to masculine and singular."

Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) said in explaining this noble verse, clarifying some of the verses that clarify what is meant by man's contention in the noble verse, after he cited his chain (sanad) to Ibn Zayd regarding His saying: ﴿but man has been most contentious of things﴾, he said: "Al-jadal is contention: the contention of peoples with their prophets and their rejection of what they brought," and he recited: ﴿This is not but a human like you; he eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:33], and he recited: ﴿He wants to make himself superior over you﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:24], and he recited up to His saying "until he died," the verse ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper, and they touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is not but obvious magic"﴾ [al-An'am 6:7], and he recited: ﴿And even if We opened for them a door from the sky, and they continued to ascend through it, they would say, "Our eyes have only been intoxicated; rather, we are a people bewitched"﴾ [al-Hijr 15:14-15]. End of quotation from the Tafsir of al-Tabari. There is no doubt that these verses which Ibn Zayd mentioned as explaining the man's contention in the verse are indeed so, as we have already said that this is the apparent context and the occasion of revelation. The verses indicating similar meanings are very numerous in the Mighty Qur'an. And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 55:**

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, and from seeking forgiveness from their Lord, except that the way of the former peoples should befall them, or the punishment should come upon them face to face.﴾

In this noble verse there are two well-known interpretations among the scholars of knowledge, and each is supported by verses from the Book of Allah, the Exalted. In my view, one of the two is clearer than the other.

The first of them is that the meaning of the verse is: Nothing prevented the people from faith and seeking forgiveness when the Messengers came to them with clear proofs, except what had already been decided in Our knowledge, namely that they would not believe, but would persist in their disbelief until the way of the former disbelievers befalls them, and the punishment comes upon them face to face on the Day of Resurrection. According to this view, the verses indicating this meaning are very numerous, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96-97]; His saying: ﴿But signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101]; and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those He leads astray, and they will have no helpers﴾ [An-Nahl: 37] (p-304). Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever Allah intends to test, you will not avail him against Allah at all. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not intend to purify; for them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 41]. The verses of this meaning are numerous.

The second view is that in the noble verse there is an omitted noun (mudaf mahdhuf), its estimated form being: Nothing prevented the people from faith and seeking forgiveness except their demand that the way of the former peoples should befall them, or that the punishment should come upon them face to face.

The verses indicating their demand for destruction and punishment, out of obstinacy and wilful defiance, are very numerous. Such as His saying about the people of Shu'ayb: ﴿So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 187]; His saying about the people of Hud: ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful"﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 22]; His saying about the people of Salih: ﴿And they said, "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the messengers"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 77]; His saying about the people of Lut: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 29]; and His saying about the people of Nuh: ﴿They said, "O Nuh, you have argued with us and multiplied our argument, so bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful"﴾ [Hud: 32].

These verses, and others like them in the Qur'an, mention some of the way of the former peoples: that they sought the hastening of punishment out of obstinacy and wilful defiance. Allah, the Exalted, made clear that He destroyed all of them with a total punishment, such as the destruction of the people of Nuh by the flood, the people of Salih by the blast, the people of Shu'ayb by the punishment of the Day of the Canopy, the people of Hud by the barren wind, and the people of Lut by making the highest part of their towns the lowest and by sending down upon them stones of baked clay, as is detailed in the Qur'anic verses.

He also made clear in many verses that the disbelievers of this community, such as the polytheists of Quraysh, asked for punishment just as those before them had asked. His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"﴾ [Al-Anfal: 32]; and His saying: ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, hasten to us our qitt before the Day of Reckoning"﴾ [Sad: 16]. The origin of qitt is the book of the king in which the reward is written, and it came to be applied to a portion. So the meaning of ﴿hasten to us our qitt﴾ is: our portion of punishment which you claim will befall us if we do not believe you and have faith in you, like the portion that the king assigns in the qitt, which is the book of reward. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"Nor does the king al-Nu'man, on the day I meet him, in his bounty give the qutut and distribute them."

His saying "yaʾfaq" means that he prefers some over others in giving. There are many verses of this kind.

The first view is clearer to me, because what contains no estimate (taqdir) is preferable to what contains an estimate, unless there is a proof from elsewhere that establishes the omitted and estimated element. And Allah knows best. In our book *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* we have mentioned the way of reconciling His saying here: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, and from seeking forgiveness from their Lord, except that the way of the former peoples should befall them﴾ [Al-Kahf: 55], with His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [Al-Isra': 94]. Its essential point, in brief, is this: the preventing factor mentioned in Surah Al-Isra' is an ordinary (habitual) preventing factor which can be absent, because the disbeliever's amazement at Allah sending a human messenger is an ordinary preventing factor which can be absent, since it is possible that a disbeliever is amazed that a human was sent as a messenger and yet believes in him despite that amazement. Thus the restriction (hasr) in His saying: ﴿nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [Al-Isra': 94] is a restriction to the ordinary preventing factor. As for the restriction in His saying here: ﴿nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, and from seeking forgiveness from their Lord, except that the way of the former peoples should befall them, or the punishment should come upon them face to face﴾ [Al-Kahf: 55], it is a restriction to the real preventing factor, because His will, glory be to Him, that they should not believe, His judgement upon them of that, and His decree of it, is a real preventing factor from the occurrence of anything else.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿or the punishment should come upon them face to face﴾, the Kufans (ʿAsim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i) read *qubulan* with a *damma* on the *qaf* and the *ba'*. The other four of the seven readers (Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir) read *qibalan* with a *kasra* on the *qaf* and a *fatha* on the *ba'*. On the reading of the Kufans, *qubulan* with two *dammas* is the plural of *qabil*. A *fa'il* form that is a noun is pluralised on the pattern *fu'ul*, as *sarir* / *surur*, *tariq* / *turuq*, and *hasir* / *husur*, as he indicated in the *Khulasah* with his saying:

"A *fi'l* for a quadriliteral noun with a *mad* has been added before the *lam*, for *i'lal*, so it is established, unless it is doubled in the general case, the one with the *alif*."

So, according to this, the meaning of ﴿or the punishment should come upon them *qubulan*﴾ is: of various kinds, following one another. On the reading of those who read *qibalan* like *'inabin*, its meaning is "face to face", that is, or the punishment should come upon them openly before their eyes. Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, said that *qubulan* means "suddenly". The verified view is that its meaning is "face to face", and its root is from *muqabalah* (facing one another), because each of two who face each other sees the other. Abu 'Ubayd mentioned that the meanings of the two readings are one, and that their meaning is "face to face", and its root is from *muqabalah*. The accusative of *qubulan* is circumstantial (hal) on both readings. On the two stated views about the meaning of *qubulan*: if we estimate that it means "face to face", then it is an indefinite verbal noun used as a circumstantial accusative, as we have mentioned repeatedly. If it is the plural of *qabil*, then it is a fixed noun interpreted as a derived noun, because it means: or the punishment should come upon them in the state of being various kinds and types of different forms. The verbal noun formed from *an* and its clause in His saying ﴿that they should believe﴾ is in the accusative position, because it is the second object of *mana'a* (prevented). The verbal noun formed from *an* and its clause in His saying ﴿except that the way of the former peoples should befall them﴾ is in the nominative position, because it is the subject (fa'il) of *mana'a*, since the exception is *mufarragh* (an exception with no stated object), and what precedes *illa* governs what follows it. So the estimate becomes: The coming of the way of the former peoples prevented the people from faith, according to his saying in the *Khulasah*:

"If the preceding is left empty for *illa* to what comes after, it will be as if *illa* were absent."

Seeking forgiveness in His saying ﴿and seek forgiveness from their Lord﴾ is asking Him, glory be to Him, for forgiveness of all past sins, by turning back (in repentance) to Him, regret for what has passed, and a firm resolve never to return to the sin.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 56:**

Allah's saying: ﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, mentions that He sends the messengers only as bearers of good news, giving glad tidings of Paradise to those who obey them, and as warners, warning those who disobey them of the Fire. He repeats this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. Whoever believes and makes amends, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ [al-An'am: 48]. We have already explained the meaning of good news (bishara) and warning (indhar) at the beginning of this noble surah, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿to warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾ [al-Kahf: 2]. The word ﴿bearers of good news﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: We send them only while they are bearers of good news and warners.

Allah's saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute thereby the truth﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, mentions that those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood, that is, they contend with the messengers using falsehood. Examples are their saying about the Messenger: "a sorcerer, a poet, a soothsayer," and their saying about the Qur'an: "fables of the ancients, sorcery, poetry, soothsaying," and their asking about the People of the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn, and their asking about the Spirit, out of obstinacy and perversity, in order to nullify the truth by their disputing and contending with falsehood. Thus, jidal means contention, and the object of ﴿disputes﴾ is omitted, the preceding context indicating it, because His saying ﴿We send the messengers﴾ shows that those whom the disbelievers dispute with using falsehood are the messengers mentioned just above. Omitting a non-essential element when the context indicates it is permissible and occurs frequently in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech, as Ibn Malik stated in al-Khulasa (his versified grammar) with his verse:

*"The omission of a non-essential element is permissible if it causes no harm, like the omission of what is given as an answer or restricted."*

And al-batil (falsehood) is the opposite of the truth. Every thing that is transient and perishing, the Arabs call batil. From it is the saying of Labid:

*"Surely everything except Allah is false, and every bliss is certainly transient."*

The plural of batil is often given as abatil, contrary to the regular pattern, which falls under Ibn Malik's saying in al-Khulasa:

*"And whatever deviates from analogy in both sections, its ruling and form being exceptional..."*

From it is the saying of Ka'b ibn Zuhayr:

*"The promises of 'Urqub were a proverb, but his promises were nothing but falsehoods."*

It is also plural as bawatil by analogy. Al-haqq (the truth) is the opposite of falsehood, and every thing that is firm, not transient or perishing, the Arabs call haqq. Allah's saying ﴿to refute thereby the truth﴾ [al-Kahf: 56] means: to nullify it and remove it by it. Its origin is from dahd al-qadam (slipping of the foot), which is its sliding and removal from its place. The Arabs say: "his foot slipped (dahadat rijluhu)" when it slid, and "Allah made it slip (adhdahaha Allah)" means He caused it to slide. "His argument slipped (dahadat hujjatuhu)" when it became void, and "Allah made it slip (adhdahaha Allah)" means He nullified it. A place that is dahd is one where feet slip. From it is the saying of Tarafa:

*"O Abu Mundhir, you desired loyalty but you feared it, and you swerved as a camel swerves from the slippery ground."*

What he mentioned here, the disbelievers' disputing with falsehood against the messenger, he clarified in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is void in the sight of their Lord﴾ [al-Shura: 16], and His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers hate it﴾ [al-Tawbah: 32], and His saying: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers hate it﴾ [al-Saff: 8]. Their wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths is only by their contention and their disputing with falsehood.

Allah has also explained in other places that what the disbelievers wanted, namely refuting the truth with falsehood, will not happen, and that they will not attain what they wanted. Rather, what will happen is the opposite of what they wanted, so the truth is established and falsehood is nullified, as Allah said: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists hate it﴾ [al-Saff: 9], and as in His saying: ﴿And Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers hate it﴾ [al-Tawbah: 33], and His saying: ﴿And Allah perfects His light, even though the disbelievers hate it﴾ [al-Tawbah: 32], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya': 18], and His saying: ﴿And say: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾ [al-Isra': 81], and His saying: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire seeking ornament or goods is foam like it. Thus Allah strikes the example of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but what benefits people remains on the earth. Thus Allah sets forth examples﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17], and other verses indicating that the truth will manifest and rise, and that falsehood will vanish, perish, and pass away as scum. That is the opposite of what the disbelievers were seeking, namely nullifying the truth and refuting it with falsehood through contention and disputing.

Allah's saying: ﴿And they take My signs and what they are warned of in mockery﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the disbelievers took His signs, which He sent down to His Messenger, and the warning given to them, as a mockery (huzu'), that is, derision and belittling. The verbal noun (masdar) here has the meaning of the passive participle: they took them as things mocked and belittled, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned﴾ [al-Furqan: 30].

This meaning mentioned here is clarified in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿And when he learns of some of Our signs, he takes them in mockery﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 9], His saying: ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but they mock him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 30], His saying: ﴿And messengers were mocked before you, but those who scoffed at them were surrounded by what they used to mock﴾ [al-An'am: 10], and His saying: ﴿If you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing." Say: "Is it Allah and His signs and His Messenger that you were mocking?" Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 65–66], and other verses.

The word ﴿ma﴾ in His saying ﴿what they are warned of﴾ is a verbal particle (masdariyya), as we have established, and on this view there is no omitted pronoun. It has also been said that it is a relative pronoun (mawsula) with an omitted returning pronoun, the estimated sense being: "and what they were warned of by it, in mockery." The omission of a returning pronoun governed by a preposition is regular only under the conditions mentioned by Ibn Malik in al-Khulasa with his verse:

*"Likewise, the one governed by a preposition after the relative pronoun is governed, as in 'the one I passed by' — so it is correct."*

In His saying ﴿huzuwan﴾ (mockery) there are three recitations among the seven canonical readings (qira'at). Hamza recited it with the zay sukun in continuous recitation (wasl), while the remaining seven read it with a damma on the zay and the hamza realized. Except that Hafs, from 'Asim, changes the hamza into a waw, and this is transmitted from Hamza in pausal recitation (waqf).

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 57 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who has been reminded of the verses of his Lord, but turned away from them and forgot what his hands had sent forward?﴾ In this noble verse, He, glorified and exalted, mentions that there is no one more unjust, i.e., no one who wrongs himself more, than one who has been reminded, i.e., admonished, with the verses of his Lord, which is this great Qur'an. ﴿But turned away from them﴾ [al-Kahf: 57], i.e., he turned his back and averted from them.

We have said that the intended meaning of "the verses" is this great Qur'an, because of the evidence of the masculine pronoun referring to "the verses" in His saying ﴿that they understand it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, which is expressed by "the verses." It is also possible that "the verses" includes the Qur'an and other things, and the pronoun in His saying ﴿that they understand it﴾ would then refer to what was mentioned of the verses, like the saying of Ru'bah:

In it are lines of black and white,
as if upon its hide is the speckling of leprosy (bahaq).

A parallel in the Qur'an is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: Indeed, He says it is a cow neither old nor virgin, but between that﴾ [al-Baqarah: 68], i.e., that which was mentioned of the old and the virgin. A parallel from the speech of the Arabs is the saying of Ibn al-Zib'ara:

Indeed for good and for evil there is a limit,
and both of those have a face and a side.

I.e., both of those mentioned, of good and of evil. We have already explained this.

His saying ﴿and forgot what his hands had sent forward﴾ [al-Kahf: 57], i.e., of sins and disbelief, although Allah has not forgotten it, but rather He records it against him and will recompense him for it, as He said: ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allah has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it, and Allah is Witness over all things﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 6]. And He said: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that. And your Lord is never forgetful﴾ [Maryam: 64]. And He said: ﴿He said: Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Taha: 52].

Some scholars said regarding His saying ﴿and forgot what his hands had sent forward﴾ that it means he left it deliberately and did not repent of it, and al-Qurtubi, may Allah have mercy on him, began his commentary with this view. What He mentioned in this noble verse, that turning away from the reminder of Allah's verses is among the greatest injustice, He has added to it in other places an explanation of some of the bad results and grievous consequences that arise from turning away from the reminder. Among its bad results is what He mentioned here, that its bearer is among the most unjust of people. Among its bad results is the placing of coverings over the hearts so that they do not understand the truth, and never being guided, as He said here, explaining some of what arises from it of bad consequences: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness. And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. Among them is Allah's retribution, may He be exalted, upon the one who turns away from the reminder, as He said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who has been reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turned away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾ [al-Sajdah: 22]. Among them (p-310) is that the one who turns away is like a donkey, as He said: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder, as if they were startled donkeys fleeing﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 49-50], the verse. Among them is the warning of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud, as He said: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾ [Fussilat: 13], the verse. Among them is a constricted life and blindness, as He said: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ [Taha: 124]. Among them is His making him enter a severe punishment, as He said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will make him enter a severe punishment﴾ [al-Jinn: 17]. Among them is the assignment to him of companions from the devils, as He said: ﴿And whoever is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 36]. And beyond that are other bad results and grievous consequences that arise from turning away from the reminder with the verses of Allah, may He be exalted.

He, may He be exalted, has commanded in another place to turn away from the one who turns his back on His remembrance, whose outlook is limited to the life of this world, and He made clear that this is the extent of his knowledge, so he has no knowledge of what would benefit him in his return. That is in His saying: ﴿So turn away from one who has turned his back on Our remembrance and desires nothing but the worldly life. That is the extent of their knowledge﴾ [al-Najm: 29-30]. He, glorified and exalted, has also forbidden obeying the like of that one who turns his back on the remembrance and is heedless of it, in His saying: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his desire and whose affair has been [ever] neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28], as has already been explained.

His saying in this verse ﴿what his hands had sent forward﴾, i.e., what he had sent forward of deeds of disbelief. The attribution of "sending forward" specifically to the hand is because the hand is the organ that most often performs deeds, more than other limbs, so deeds are attributed to it according to the custom of the Arabs in their speech. Even if some of the deeds he sent forward are not done by the hand, such as disbelief with the tongue and the heart, and other deeds that are not performed by the hand, such as fornication. We have explained in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) the way of reconciling His saying ﴿And who is more unjust than one who has been reminded of the verses of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 57], the verse, with His saying ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ [Hud: 18], and similar verses.

The best-known ways of reconciling this are two. The first is that everyone of whom Allah says "And who is more unjust than one who did such and such?" means that there is no one more unjust than any single one of them. Thus they are equal in injustice, none of them surpassing another in it, and there is no difficulty in each of them being the one than whom no one is more unjust. The second is that the relative clause determines each one in its own place. Accordingly, the meaning of His saying ﴿And who is more unjust than one who has been reminded of the verses of his Lord, but turned away from them﴾ [al-Kahf: 57] is: there is no one more unjust than one who has been reminded and turned away, and more unjust than one who has been reminded with the verses of his Lord (p-311) and turned away from them. And His saying ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ [Hud: 18] means: there is no one among the fabricators more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah. The first is more preferable, since it follows the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and has no difficulty, and this is the view that Abu Hayyan chose in al-Bahr.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness﴾.

In this noble verse, He, glorified and exalted, mentions that He has placed over the hearts of the wrongdoers who turn away from the verses of Allah, when they are reminded with them, coverings, i.e., veils that cover their hearts and prevent them from perceiving what would benefit them of what they were reminded with. The singular of "coverings" (akinnah) is kinan, which is a covering. He also placed in their ears a deafness (waqr), i.e., a heaviness that prevents them from hearing what would benefit them of the verses with which they were reminded. Allah has clarified this meaning in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿Allah has sealed over their hearts and over their hearing, and over their vision is a veil﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7], and His saying: ﴿Have you seen one who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly, and has sealed over his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a veil?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23], the verse. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier. And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn back on their backs in aversion﴾ [al-Isra': 45-46]. And His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He has deafened them and blinded their vision﴾ [Muhammad: 23]. And His saying: ﴿They were not able to hear, nor did they used to see﴾ [Hud: 20]. The verses of this kind are very numerous.

If it is said: If they are unable to hear, see, or understand, because Allah has placed the coverings that prevent understanding over their hearts, and the heaviness, which is the weight that prevents hearing, in their ears, then they are compelled. So what is the justification for punishing them for something they are unable to turn away from and redirect to something else?

The answer: Allah, may He be exalted, has explained in many verses of His great Book that those barriers which He places over their hearts, hearing, and sight, such as sealing, stamping, veiling, and coverings, and the like, He placed upon them only as a recompense in proportion to what they hastened to of disbelief and denial of the messengers by their own choice. So Allah turned their hearts aside through stamping and coverings and the like, as recompense for their disbelief. Among the verses that indicate this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, Allah has stamped over them because of their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa': 155], i.e., because of their disbelief. This is an explicit Qur'anic text that their prior disbelief is the cause of the stamping over their hearts. And His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5].

(p-312) This is also clear evidence that the cause of Allah's causing their hearts to deviate is their prior deviation. And His saying: ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 3]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10], the verse. And His saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am: 110]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14], and other verses indicating that the stamping over the hearts and preventing them from understanding what benefits them is a punishment from Allah for prior disbelief.

This which we have mentioned is the way of refuting the doubt of the Jabriyyah (those who deny human choice and hold that man is compelled), which they cling to in these mentioned verses and their like in the mighty Qur'an. By this which we have established, the answer is also obtained to a question that occurs to the seeker of knowledge regarding what we have established. It is this: You have already explained, in discussing the preceding verse, that the placing of coverings over the hearts is one of the results of turning away from the verses of Allah when they are reminded with them. Yet the apparent meaning of this verse indicates the opposite, namely that the aforementioned turning away has as its cause the placing of coverings over the hearts, because "inna" (indeed) is one of the particles of causation, as has been established in the principles (usul) in the mode of indication and alerting, like your saying: "Cut off his hand, indeed he is a thief," and "Punish him, indeed he is a wrongdoer." The meaning is: cut off his hand for the reason of his theft, and punish him for the reason of his wrongdoing. Likewise His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So he turned away from them and forgot what his hands had sent forward. Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ [al-Kahf: 57], i.e., he turned away from them for the reason of Our placing coverings over their hearts. This is because the preceding verses indicated that the stamping, which is expressed at times by "stamping," at times by "sealing," at times by "coverings," and the like, has as its first cause turning away from the verses of Allah and disbelief in them, as has already been explained.

In this noble verse there are two well-known questions. The first: What is the referent of the pronoun in His saying ﴿that they understand it﴾? We have already stated that it is "the verses" in His saying ﴿reminded with the verses of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 57], by including in "the verses" the meaning of the Qur'an. So His saying ﴿that they understand it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, which is expressed by "the verses," as has already been explained shortly before.

The second question: What is the reason for the singular pronoun in His saying ﴿reminded﴾, and His saying ﴿turned away from them﴾, and His saying ﴿and forgot what his hands had sent forward﴾, while the pronoun in His saying ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness﴾ is in the plural form, even though the referent of all the mentioned pronouns is one, namely the relative pronoun in His saying ﴿of one who has been reminded with the verses of his Lord﴾, the verse.

(p-213) The answer is that the singular form is based on the wording of "man" (مَن), while the plural is based on its meaning. This occurs frequently in the Great Qur'an. The correct position regarding such cases is that it is permissible to observe the wording at one time and the meaning at another time, without restriction. This differs from those who claimed that observing the wording after observing the meaning is not valid. The evidence for the validity of the view is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him provision﴾ [al-Talaq: 11]. In this noble verse, He observed the wording of "man" first, so He used the singular pronoun in His words "yu'min" (believes), "wa-ya'mal" (does), and "yudkhilhu" (admits him). Then He observed the meaning in His words "khalidina" (abiding), so He used the plural form there. Then He observed the wording again after that in His words "qad ahsana Allahu lahu rizqan" (Allah has certainly perfected for him provision).

His words "an yafqahuhu" (that they understand it) contain, and in every similar expression, two well-known interpretations among the scholars of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis):
One: the meaning is "We have placed over their hearts coverings so that they do not understand it." According to this, the negative particle "la" is omitted, its omission indicated by the context. This is the view that al-Tabari (Ibn Jarir al-Tabari) adopted here.
Two: the meaning is "We have placed over their hearts coverings out of dislike that they should understand it." According to this, the sentence has an omitted noun (a construction with an implied word, "karahat" – out of dislike). Such verses in the Qur'an are numerous, and for all of them scholars hold the two interpretations mentioned, such as His words: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [al-Nisa': 176], meaning "lest you go astray" or "out of dislike that you go astray." Also His words: ﴿If a defiant one brings you a report, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance﴾ [al-Hujurat: 6], meaning "lest you harm" or "out of dislike that you harm." Similar examples are numerous in the Great Qur'an.

His words, the Exalted, "an yafqahuhu" (that they understand it): i.e., that they comprehend it. So "al-fiqh" means understanding. From it is His words, the Exalted: ﴿So what is [wrong] with these people that they hardly understand any statement?﴾ [al-Nisa': 78], i.e., they hardly comprehend it. And His words, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say"﴾ [Hud: 91], i.e., we do not comprehend it. "Al-waqr" means heaviness. Al-Jawhari said in his Sihah: "al-waqr" with a fatha means heaviness in the ear, and "al-wiqr" with a kasra means a load; it is said, "He came carrying his wiqr," and "he loaded his camel (awqara ba'iraho)." Its most common use is for the load of a mule or donkey. End of quotation. What al-Jawhari and others mentioned has come in the Qur'an. He said regarding heaviness of the ear: ﴿And in their ears is deafness (waqr)﴾ [al-An'am: 25], and regarding a load: ﴿And those who carry the heavy load (wiqr)﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 2].

* *

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever.﴾

In this noble verse He clarifies that those upon whose hearts Allah has placed coverings, preventing them from understanding the beneficial verses of the Qur'an by which they were admonished, will never be guided. Therefore your call to them to guidance will not benefit them. This meaning to which He alludes here, that whom Allah has made wretched, admonition will not benefit, has come explained in other places, such as His words: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96]. And His words, the Exalted: ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals. They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 200]. And His words, the Exalted: ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101]. And His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah, and He places defilement upon those who do not reason﴾ [Yunus: 100]. And His words, the Exalted: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those who mislead, and they will have no helpers﴾ [al-Nahl: 37]. This verse and its like in the Qur'an have two well-known interpretations among the scholars:

One: that it concerns those for whom it has already been decreed in the knowledge of Allah that they are wretched, we seek refuge in Allah, the Exalted.

The second: that what is meant is that they are thus so long as they remain clad in disbelief. If Allah guides them to faith and they turn back in repentance, that barrier is removed. The first is more apparent, and knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

The particle "fa" (then) in His words: ﴿then they will never be guided﴾ [al-Kahf: 57] is because the verb that follows "lan" (never) cannot be a condition for "in" (if) and its like. When the consequent (jaza') is not suitable to be a condition for "in" and its like, its connection with "fa" becomes obligatory, as he (Ibn Malik) stated in the Khulasa (the Alfiyya) with his words:

"Attach with 'fa' necessarily a response, if it were made a condition for 'in' or other than it, it would not be made one."

His words in this noble verse, "idhan" (then), are the consequent and the response. It indicates the non-occurrence of their being guided by the call of the Messenger (ﷺ). The meaning is that they have made what should be a cause of guidance a cause of its absence, because the meaning is: "then they will never be guided if you call them." Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this meaning, and Abu Hayyan followed him in al-Bahr. This meaning is erroneous, and countless numbers of rhetoricians and others have erred in it.

The clarification of this is that al-Zamakhshari here and Abu Hayyan thought that His words: ﴿And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, then, ever﴾ are a condition and a consequent, and that the consequent is arranged upon the condition in the way that a consequent is arranged upon what is its condition. Therefore they thought that the consequent, which is the non-guidance expressed in the verse by His words "fa-lan yahtadu" (they will never be guided), is arranged upon the condition, which is his call to them expressed in the verse by His words "wa-in tad'uhum ila al-huda" (if you invite them to guidance), also indicated by "idhan" (then).
