Ibn Hajar said: "This came from Ibn Shawdhab, which al-Tabari recorded with a good chain of narration, through the narration of Damrah ibn Rabi'ah from Ibn Shawdhab." It is also said that he was of the descendants of one of those who believed in Ibrahim and emigrated with him from the land of Babel, related by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his History. It is also said that his father was Persian and his mother Roman, and it is said the reverse of that. [End of Ibn Hajar's quotation.] And Allah knows best the reality of the matter. It has been established in the Sahih, from the Prophet (ﷺ), through the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that he said: "He was only named al-Khidr because he sat upon a white farwah (patch of land), and behold, it would shake behind him, green." The farwah al-bayda' (white farwah) is what is on the surface of the earth of white dry grass and the like, and of dried stubble. It is also said that the farwah is the white land in which there is no vegetation, and it is said that it is dry stubble.

And of this kind is calling the scalp of the head a farwah, as we mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, in the words of the poet:

"Dirty of garments, as if the farwah of his head
Were planted, and its two sides grew pepper."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 77:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they found in it a wall about to collapse, so he set it upright﴾

, This noble verse is among the greatest proofs used by those who claim that there is metaphor (majaz) in the Qur'an. They assert that the wall's wanting to collapse (al-infiqad) cannot be taken literally, and that it is merely a metaphor. But verses from the Book of Allah show that there is no obstacle to the wall's wanting being literal, because Allah, exalted is He, gives inanimate objects (al-jamadat) wills, actions and speech that creation cannot perceive. He, exalted is He, has explicitly stated that He knows of these things what His creation does not know, in His saying, majestic and exalted is He: ﴿And there is nothing that does not exalt His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra': 44]. He thus declared that we do not understand their glorification, and their glorification proceeds from a will they have which He, exalted is He, knows and which we do not know. Similar examples are numerous in the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, among stones are those from which rivers gush forth, and indeed, among them are those that split and water comes out of them, and indeed, among them are those that fall down out of fear of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74], up to the end of the verse. His explicit statement that some stones fall down out of fear of Allah is clear evidence of this, because that fear is a form of perception which Allah knows and which we do not know. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], up to the end of the verse. His explicit statement, majestic and exalted is He, that the heaven, the earth and the mountains refused and feared (ashfaqna), i.e., were afraid, is evidence that this occurs by a will and perception which He, exalted is He, knows and which we do not know.

Among the hadiths indicating this is what is established in Sahih Muslim: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, I know a stone that used to greet me in Makkah." And what is established in Sahih al-Bukhari concerning the trunk of the palm tree on which the Prophet ﷺ used to deliver the sermon, which moaned out of longing for his separation. The greeting of that stone and the moaning of that trunk both proceed from a will and perception which Allah knows and which we do not know, just as He declared the like in His saying: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra': 44]. The claim of one who has no knowledge that these matters have no reality and are merely parables is a false claim, because the texts of the Book and the Sunnah may not be diverted from their clear and immediately understood meaning except by a proof to which one must return. Examples of this are very numerous. By this you know that there is no obstacle to keeping the wall's wanting on its literal reality, since it is possible that Allah knew from it a wanting to collapse, even if His creation did not know that will. This is very clear, as you see. Moreover, it is among the Arabic styles to use "wanting" for approaching and inclining toward something, as in the words of the poet:

"In a desert waste, whose heads (of camels) were agitated by it, like the agitation of axes when they wanted to cut (nudul)."

So his saying "idha aradna nudulan" means: when they approached it. And the saying of another:

"The spear wants the chest of Abu Bara'," and turns away from the blood of Bani 'Uqayl.

That is: it inclines toward the chest of Abu Bara'. And like the saying of the shepherd of Numayr:

"Indeed, a time that gathers my scattered affairs with a camel-herd is a time that intends kindness."

So his saying "a time that intends kindness" (yahumm bil-ihsan). We have explained in our treatise entitled "Man' Jawaz al-Majaz fi al-Manzil lil-Ta'abbud wal-I'jaz" that all the verses which they claim to be metaphor, none of them is specifically metaphorical, and we explained the proofs for this. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every boat by force﴾

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that this king seizes every boat, whether sound or defective. But it is understood from another verse that he does not seize the defective one, which is His saying: ﴿So I wished to make it defective﴾ [al-Kahf: 79], meaning, so that he would not seize it. This is the wisdom in his (al-Khadir's) damaging it, mentioned in His saying: ﴿Until, when they boarded the boat, he damaged it﴾ [al-Kahf: 71]. Then he explained that his purpose in damaging it was to preserve it for its people from the seizure of that usurping king, because its defect would make him disinclined to it. For the reason we have mentioned, this noble verse is an example, among the scholars of Arabic grammar, of the omission of the qualifier (naʿt), meaning: "And there was behind them a king who seized every sound boat, not defective, by the evidence we have mentioned."

We have already presented the Arabic evidence for this in the surah "Banu Isra'il" in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is not a town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment﴾ [al-Isra': 58], and the name of that king is Hudad ibn Badr. His saying ﴿behind them﴾ means "in front of them," as was mentioned earlier in the surah "Ibrahim."

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So I wished to make it defective﴾.

This verse indicates that its defect would be a cause for the usurping king to leave it, and for this reason al-Khadir damaged it. The generality of His saying: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every boat by force﴾ [al-Kahf: 79] requires that the king seize both the defective and the sound.

The answer is that there is an omission of the qualifier in the speech, and its estimated form is "every boat that is fit and sound." The omission of the qualifier is permissible when the context indicates it, as Ibn Malik indicated in al-Khulasa with his saying:

"What is understood of the modified and the modifier may be omitted, and omission of the modifier is rare."

Among the evidence for the omission of the qualifier is the saying of the poet:

"And many a fair-cheeked virgin with a soft-curved neck and dark hair falls to her..."

meaning: she has jet-black hair and a long neck.

And the saying of 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras al-Usayyidi:

"From his speech is speech, and from his deed is deed, and from his bounty is bounty."

meaning: from his speech is decisive speech, from his deed is a beautiful deed, and from his bounty is a generous bounty.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of black mud﴾

Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Hafs from 'Asim read "ḥami'atin" (حَمِئَةٍ) without an alif after the ḥa', and with a fatḥah-marked hamza after the kasra-marked mim. Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Shu'bah from 'Asim read "ḥamiyatin" (حامِيَةٍ) with an alif after the ḥa', and a fatḥah-marked ya' after the kasra-marked mim, in the form of the active participle (ism al-fa'il). According to the first reading, the meaning of "ḥami'atin" is "possessing ḥama'ah," and ḥama'ah is black mud. This interpretation is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We created man from clay of black mud, molded﴾ [al-Hijr: 26]. And ḥama' is mud, as has already been explained. From this meaning is the saying of Tubba' al-Himyari, as it is transmitted from him, praising Dhu al-Qarnayn:

"He reached the easts and the wests, seeking the means of a matter from a wise, guiding one,

So he saw the setting of the sun at its sinking, in a spring of mud (dhi khalab) and black slime (tha'ṭ ḥarmad)."

Al-khalab, in the dialect of Himyar, is mud; al-tha'ṭ is ḥama'ah; and al-ḥarmad is black. According to the reading "ḥamiyatin" in the form of the active participle, the meaning is that it is hot, because of its proximity to the blaze of the sun at its setting and its meeting the rays without any barrier. There is no contradiction between the two readings, and both are true. Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir: ﴿and he found it setting in a spring of black mud﴾ [al-Kahf: 86], i.e., he saw the sun, in his view, setting into the Atlantic Ocean, and this is the case of everyone who reaches its shore, seeing it as though it sets into it, until the end of his words. The implication of his words is that what is meant by "'ayn" in the verse is the Atlantic Ocean, which has black mud. In the language, "'ayn" is applied to a spring of water, and al-yanbu' is abundant water, so the name "'ayn" linguistically applies to the sea. And that one on the shore of the western Ocean sees the sun, in the perception of his eye, falling into the sea is a well-known matter. On this interpretation there is no difficulty in the verse, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 98 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true."﴾ ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering.﴾

Know first that we have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that if some verses have an explanation within the Qur'an that does not fully clarify the intended meaning, and the Prophet (ﷺ) has explained it, then we complete its explanation by citing the Sunnah that explains it. We have already given many examples of this. Once you know that, know that these two verses have an explanation from the Book that the Sunnah has made clear. Thus, with the addition of the Sunnah to the Qur'an, it becomes a complete explanation of the intended meaning. Almighty and Exalted God said in His Book to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder, that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them, and that they may reflect﴾ [al-Nahl: 44]. Once you know that, know that this noble verse and the verse in al-Anbiya' have in general indicated that the barrier which Dhu al-Qarnayn built is not destroyed by Gog and Magog, but rather God will make it level (dakk) when the appointed time for that comes. Both verses also indicate that this is close to the Day of Resurrection, because He said here: ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true.﴾ ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Kahf: 98–99]. The most apparent of the opinions regarding the omitted clause for which the tanwin of "yawma'idhin" is a substitute, from His saying: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾, is that it means: the day when the promise of my Lord comes, with their emergence and dispersal over the earth. One should not deviate from this view, since it agrees with the apparent context of the Mighty Qur'an. Once it is established that the meaning of "yawma'idhin" is "the day when the promise comes with their emergence and dispersal," know that the pronoun in His saying ﴿some of them﴾, according to the view that it refers to all the children of Adam, means the Day of Resurrection. In that case, the verse indicates that it is associated with their emergence when the barrier is leveled, and close to it. According to the view that the pronoun refers to Gog and Magog, His saying after it, ﴿and the Horn will be blown﴾, indicates in general that it is near to it. Al-Zamakhshari said in his tafsir of this verse, ﴿He said, "This is a mercy from my Lord,"﴾ that it refers to the barrier: that is, this barrier is a blessing from God and a mercy upon His servants, or this empowerment and enablement to level it. ﴿But when the promise of my Lord comes﴾, meaning, when the coming of the Day of Resurrection draws near and is about to arrive, He will make the barrier level (dakk), that is, leveled, spread out, made even with the ground. Anything that spreads out after being raised is leveled (indakka), and from this comes the camel with a level hump (al-jamal al-adakk), whose hump is flattened. End of quotation.

The verse of al-Anbiya' referred to is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they swarm from every elevation﴾ ﴿and the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Anbiya': 96–97]. This is because His saying, ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released﴾, and its being followed by His saying, ﴿and the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾, indicates in general what we mentioned in the tafsir of the verse of al-Kahf that we are now discussing. This indicates the invalidity of the view of those who claim that they are the Russians and that the barrier was opened a long time ago. If it is said: the aforementioned verses in al-Kahf and al-Anbiya' only indicate the general nearness of the Day of Resurrection to the leveling of the barrier, and its nearness to the Day of Resurrection does not preclude that it has already occurred in fact, as God the Exalted said: ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near to them﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Anbiya': 1], and He said: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar: 1], and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a breach has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this," and he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. (The hadith continues.) We have already mentioned this in surah al-Ma'idah. The Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah thus indicate that the drawing near of such things does not necessitate their being associated with it; rather, it is valid for it to draw near with an interval. Accordingly, the supposed past leveling of the barrier does not contradict the nearness to the Day of Resurrection, and there is no evidence in the aforementioned verses that the barrier has not been leveled until now.

The answer: it is what we have mentioned, that this explanation by these verses is not fully complete in clarifying the matter except by adding the Sunnah to it. For this reason we said that we complete such matters from the Sunnah, since it explains the Qur'an. Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, may God have mercy on him, said in his Sahih: Abu Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to me, Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, judge of Homs, narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to me from his father Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami: that he heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi (transition) And Muhammad ibn Mihran al-Razi narrated to me, and the wording is his, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us from Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) mentioned the Dajjal one morning, and he lowered his voice regarding him and raised it, until we thought him to be in the group of palm trees. When we went to him, he perceived that in us and said: 'What is the matter with you?' We said: 'O Messenger of God, you mentioned the Dajjal this morning and lowered your voice and raised it, until we thought him to be in the group of palm trees.' He said: 'What I fear for you is other than the Dajjal. If he emerges while I am among you, I will be his opponent on your behalf. If he emerges while I am not among you, each man will be his own opponent, and God is my successor over every Muslim. He is a young man with curly hair, his eye is blind, and I liken him to Abd al-Uzza ibn Qatan. Whoever of you meets him, let him recite over him the opening verses of surah al-Kahf. He will emerge from a passage between Syria and Iraq, and he will wreak havoc right and left. O servants of God, remain steadfast.' We said: 'O Messenger of God, how long will he remain on the earth?' He said: 'Forty days: one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and his other days are like your days.' We said: 'O Messenger of God, on that day which is like a year, would one prayer of a day suffice us?' He said: 'No, estimate its measure.' We said: 'O Messenger of God, how swift will his passage be upon the earth?' He said: 'Like rain driven before the wind.' He will come upon a people and call them, and they will believe in him and respond to him. He will command the sky and it will rain, and the earth and it will produce, and their herds will return to them at their longest, fullest of udders and most distended of flanks. Then he will come to another people and call them, and they will reject his word, and he will depart from them, and they will wake up in drought with nothing of their wealth in their hands. He will pass by a ruin and say to it: 'Bring forth your treasures,' and its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees. Then he will call a young man full of vigor, and strike him with the sword and cut him into two pieces, the distance of an arrow's throw from a target. Then he will call him, and he will come forward with a radiant face, smiling. While he is in this state, God will send the Messiah, son of Mary, and he will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two garments dyed with saffron, placing his palms on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, drops fall, and when he raises it, pearls like jewels pour from it. No disbeliever who smells his breath will live, and his breath reaches as far as his gaze. He will seek the Dajjal until he overtakes him at the gate of Lud and kills him. Then Jesus son of Mary will come to a people whom God has protected from him, and he will wipe their faces and tell them of their ranks in Paradise. While he is in this state, God reveals to Jesus: 'I have brought forth servants of Mine, no one has the power to fight them, so bring My servants into the mount (al-Tur).' God will send forth Gog and Magog, and they will swarm from every elevation. The first of them will pass by the Lake of Tiberias and drink what is in it, and the last of them will pass by and say: 'There was once water here.' The Prophet of God, Jesus, and his companions will be besieged, until the head of an ox is better for one of them than a hundred dinars is for one of you today. The Prophet of God, Jesus, and his companions will beseech God, and God will send upon them the worm (al-nagaf) in their necks, and they will wake up dead as one soul. Then the Prophet of God, Jesus, and his companions will descend to the earth, and they will find no place on the earth the span of a hand that is not filled with their putrefaction and stench. The Prophet of God, Jesus, and his companions will beseech God, and God will send birds like the necks of Bactrian camels, and they will carry them and cast them where God wills. Then God will send a rain which no house of clay or hair will shelter from, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a mirror. Then it will be said to the earth: 'Bring forth your fruit and return your blessing.' On that day a company will eat from a pomegranate and shelter under its peel. Blessing will be placed upon milk, so that a she-camel's milk will suffice a large group of people, a cow's milk will suffice a tribe, and a sheep's milk will suffice a clan. While they are in this state, God will send a pleasant wind which will take them under their armpits and seize the soul of every believer and every Muslim, and the wicked of mankind will remain, copulating openly like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will come.'" Ended, with its wording, from the Sahih of Muslim, may God the Exalted have mercy on him.

You have seen in this authentic hadith the explicit statement of the Prophet (ﷺ) that God reveals to Jesus son of Mary the emergence of Gog and Magog after his killing of the Dajjal. Therefore whoever claims that they are the Russians, and that the barrier was leveled long ago, opposes what the Prophet (ﷺ) has reported in a clear opposition for which there is no justification. There is no doubt that every report contradicting the report of the truthful and believed one (ﷺ) is false, because the contradictory of a truthful report is necessarily false, as is well known. Nothing has been established in the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Prophet (ﷺ) that opposes this hadith, whose chain of transmission you have seen to be sound and whose clear indication of the intended meaning is evident.

The true foundation for those who claim that Gog and Magog are the Russians, and for those among the atheists who claim that they do not exist at all, is in their own view an intellectual argument. According to what is established in dialectic, it is a conditional syllogism (qiyas istithna'i) composed of a connected conditional proposition (shartiyyah muttasilah luzumiyyah) in the view of the one who argues with it, in which the negation of the consequent is stated, so that the negation of the antecedent follows. Its form of arrangement is that one says: If Gog and Magog were behind the barrier until now, people would have discovered them because of the development of the means of communication; but no one has discovered them. Therefore they are not behind the barrier until now, because the stating of the negation of the consequent produces the negation of the antecedent, as is well known. In plainer terms for the non-logician: the negation of the necessary consequence entails the negation of that which necessitates it. This is the foundation of the argument of those who deny their existence behind the barrier until now. It is well known that the conditional syllogism known as the shartī, when composed of a connected conditional and a stated premise, is open to objection from three aspects:

The first: that it be refuted from the aspect of its being conditional, because the link between the antecedent and the consequent is not valid.

The second: that it be refuted from the aspect of its being a stated (istithna'i) syllogism.

The third possibility: that the argument is challenged from both of their sides together. This alleged syllogism is challenged from the side of its conditional form. One says to the objector: the connection between the antecedent and the consequent here is not valid. Your statement, "If they were existing behind the barrier until now, people would have come to know of them," is not valid, because it is possible that they exist while God hides their place from the general population until the appointed time arrives for bringing them out to the people. What supports the possibility of this is what God Most High mentioned in Surah "al-Ma'idah," that He made the Children of Israel wander in the land for forty years. This is in His saying, Most High: ﴿He said: "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 26]. They were in a small number of farsakhs of the land, walking by night and day, and the people did not come to know of them until the period of the wandering ended, because if they had gathered with the people, they would have shown them the way. In any case, "your Lord is the Doer of what He intends." The reports of His Messenger ﷺ that are established from him are true. As for what exists among the People of the Book that contradicts what we have mentioned, and similar stories transmitted that are in the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah, claiming that it is revealed in the Torah or other heavenly books, it is certainly false and not to be relied upon by us. This is because God, Majestic and Exalted, has declared in this Great Qur'an, "which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it, a revelation from One who is Wise and Praiseworthy," that they altered, distorted and changed their books, as in His saying: ﴿They distort words from their places﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13], and His saying: ﴿You make them into scattered pages, showing some and concealing much﴾ [al-An'am: 91], and His saying: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," to exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79], and His saying, Most High: ﴿And indeed, among them is a party who distort their tongues with the Book, that you may think it is from the Book, and it is not from the Book. And they say, "It is from Allah," and it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know it﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 78], (p-346) and other verses besides these. This is in contrast to this Great Qur'an, for God Most High has Himself undertaken its preservation, and no one has been able to alter it, change it, or distort it, as He Most High said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]. He said: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16-17]. He said: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it﴾ [Fussilat: 42]. He said concerning the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [al-Najm: 3-4]. It is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he permitted his Ummah to narrate from the Children of Israel, and forbade them from believing them or denying them, lest they believe in falsehood or deny the truth.

It is known that what is related from the Children of Israel, the reports known as the Isra'iliyyat, has three states. In one of them it is obligatory to affirm it, which is when the Book or the established Sunnah indicates its truthfulness. In one it is obligatory to reject it, which is when the Qur'an or the Sunnah likewise indicates its falsehood. In the third it is permissible neither to reject nor to affirm, as in the hadith referred to just above: which is when neither its truthfulness nor its falsehood is established in a Book or a Sunnah. By this verification you know that the stories that contradict the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah, which are attributed by some of them, claiming that they are in the revealed books, must be rejected for contradicting the texts of authentic revelation, which were not altered or changed. And God knows best.

As for His saying, Most High, in this noble verse: ﴿He made it crumbled (dakka'a)﴾: Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read "dakkan" with tanwin, as a verbal noun of "dakkahu" (he leveled it). 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿dakka'a﴾ with the feminine long alif, as the feminine form of "adakk" (flat). The meanings of the two readings return to one thing, and we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 100:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, exposed.﴾

His saying: ﴿And We will present﴾, i.e., We will bring forth and make manifest Hell ﴿that Day﴾, i.e., the day when We gather them in a gathering, as His saying before it indicates: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering﴾ [al-Kahf: 99]. Some scholars said: the lam in His saying "for the disbelievers" carries the meaning of ʿalā (upon), i.e., We will present Hell upon the disbelievers. The Qur'an supports this in several verses, because ʿarḍ (presentation) in the Qur'an is followed by ʿalā, not by lam, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are presented to the Fire﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 20], and His saying: ﴿The Fire, they are presented to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir: 46], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾ [al-Kahf: 48]. (p-347) Its parallel in the speech of the Arabs, where lam is used with the meaning of "ʿalā," is the line of verse that we cited at the beginning of surah Hud, and we mentioned the disagreement over its speaker, which is his saying:

"I pierced him with the spear through the collar of his shirt, so he fell prostrate upon both hands and the mouth."

i.e., he fell prostrate upon the two hands.

It is known from these verses that the Fire is presented to them and they are presented to it, because it is brought near to them and they are brought near to it. As He, may He be exalted, said regarding its presentation to them here: ﴿And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, exposed﴾ [al-Kahf: 100], and He said regarding their presentation to it: ﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are presented to the Fire﴾, the verse [al-Ahqaf: 34], and similar verses. We have explained some of the attributes of their presentation, which other verses of the Book of Allah indicate, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾ [al-Kahf: 48]. As for the view of one who said that His saying here, ﴿And We will present Hell﴾, the verse [al-Kahf: 100], contains an inversion (qalb), and that the meaning is: "And We will present the disbelievers to Hell," i.e., upon it, it is far-fetched, as Abu Hayyan clarified in al-Bahr. And Allah knows best.

The verified position regarding His words, ﴿Those whose eyes were under a veil from My remembrance, and who could not hear﴾, is that it is in the genitive position (mahall khafd, i.e. grammatically in the genitive case) as a qualifier (na't) of "the disbelievers." In this noble verse, the Almighty has explained that among the characteristics of the disbelievers who will be presented to Hell on the Day of Resurrection is that in the worldly life their eyes were under a veil from His remembrance, the Exalted, and they could not hear. He has explained this characteristic of theirs in many verses, such as His words concerning the covering of their eyes: ﴿And over their sight is a veil﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7], and His words: ﴿And He has placed over his sight a veil﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23], and His words: ﴿Is then one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 19], and His words: ﴿Nor are the blind and the seeing alike﴾ [Fatir: 19]. The verses of this kind are very numerous. Concerning their inability to hear, He said: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He has deafened them and blinded their vision﴾ [Muhammad: 23], and He said: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. We have already explained the meaning of their being unable to hear at the beginning of Surah "Hud," in the discussion of His words: ﴿Their punishment will be doubled. They could not bear to hear, nor did they see﴾ [Hud: 20], so there is no need to repeat it here. We have also explained a portion of this in the discussion of His words in this noble surah: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. (p-348) The Exalted has also explained in another place that the aforementioned veil, by which the sight is blinded to His remembrance, is such that Allah assigns to its possessor a devil who becomes his companion, and that is in His words: ﴿And whoever turns blindly away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 36].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 102:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors instead of Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers.﴾

The hamza in His saying, ﴿Do ... think﴾ (afahasiba) is for denunciation and rebuke. In the verse there is an ellipsis (hadhf) that the context indicates. Some scholars said: the estimated omitted part is: "Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors instead of Me, and that I will not punish them with a severe punishment? No! Rather, I will punish them for that with a severe punishment," as evidenced by His saying after it: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a lodging for the disbelievers﴾ [al-Kahf: 102]. Other scholars said: its estimate is: "Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors instead of Me, and that this will benefit them? No, it will not benefit them, but it will harm them." This is supported by His saying about them: ﴿We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ [az-Zumar: 3], and His saying about them: ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 18]. Then He, may He be exalted, made the falsehood of that clear in His saying: ﴿Say, "Will you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth? Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him"﴾ [Yunus: 18]. What He denounced them for here, namely their thinking that they could take protectors from His servants instead of Him, without Him punishing them, or that this would benefit them, has been explained in many places, such as His saying at the beginning of surah al-A'raf: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord and do not follow other than Him as protectors﴾ [al-A'raf: 3]. He forbade them from following protectors other than Him in this verse, because such protectors harm them and do not benefit them. Similar proofs are numerous in the Qur'an that there is no protector (wali) other than Allah for anyone, and that loyalty (muwalah) is only for the sake of Allah, such as His saying: ﴿See how well He hears and sees! They have no protector other than Him﴾ [al-Kahf: 26]; His saying: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have wronged, lest the Fire touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah; then you would not be helped﴾ [Hud: 113]; His saying: ﴿And whom Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector﴾ [ash-Shura: 44]; His saying: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, having besides Him no protector﴾ [al-An'am: 51]; His saying: ﴿And remind with it, lest a soul be held in pledge for what it has earned, having besides Allah no protector﴾ [al-An'am: 70], and similar verses. He will, if Allah wills, provide further clarification and examples shortly.

The most apparent and immediately understood meaning of the idafah in His saying "My servants" is that they refer to beings such as the angels, 'Isa and 'Uzayr, not the devils and the like, because such an idafah is generally for honour (tashrif). Allah has made clear that these will not be protectors for them in His saying: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, then say to the angels, "Did these worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our Protector, not them"﴾ [Saba': 40-41]. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared﴾ [al-Kahf: 102], we have already clarified its meaning in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire﴾ [al-Kahf: 29], so there is no need to repeat it here.

Regarding His saying "nuzulan" (as a lodging), scholars have several interpretations, the most apparent of which is that "nuzul" is what is prepared for a guest upon his arrival, and for one who arrives upon his coming. The meaning is that what is prepared for them of honour upon their coming to their Lord is Hell, which is prepared for them, as in His saying: ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 24], and His saying: ﴿They will be given relief with water like murky oil﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]. We have already presented its Arabic evidence in the discussion of His saying, ﴿They will be given relief with water like murky oil﴾, because that water which scalds the faces contains no relief, just as Hell is not a lodging of honouring a guest or an arriving person.

The second interpretation: "nuzulan" means "manzil" (a place of dwelling), i.e., "We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a manzil," meaning a place of alighting, with no other dwelling for them besides it. The weakest of the interpretations is what some claimed, that "nuzul" is the plural of "nazil," like the plural of "sharif" as "shuruf" with two dammas. What appears regarding the grammatical analysis (i'rab) of "nuzulan" is that it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) interpreted as having the sense of a derived noun (mushtaqq), or an object of "a'tadna" with its meaning being implicitly extended to "sayyarna" (We made) or "ja'alna" (We made).

And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 103 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ ﴿Those whose effort has been lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing well in work.﴾

The meaning: Say to them, O Prophet of Allah: "Shall We inform you," that is, tell you, "of the greatest losers in deeds," that is, of those who are the greatest losers among people in their deeds and the most wasted in them. Al-akhsar (the greatest loser) is an elative form (ṣīghat tafḍīl) from al-khusrān (loss), and its original sense is the reduction of a merchant's capital. In the Qur'an, it refers to their being cheated out of their share of what is with Allah, because of their disbelief and sins, had they obeyed Him. His saying ﴿in deeds﴾ (a'mālan) is in the accusative as a specification (tamyīz).

If it is said: "Inform us of the greatest losers in deeds, who are they?" the answer is: "They are those whose effort has been lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing well in work." From this you know that "those" (alladhīna) in His saying ﴿Those whose effort has been lost﴾ [Al-Kahf: 104] is the predicate of an omitted subject, an answer to the question understood from the context. It may also be in the accusative as a dispraise, or in the genitive as a substitute (badal) for "the greatest losers" or as an attribute (na't) of it. His saying ﴿whose effort has been lost﴾ means that their work has become void and ruined, so it becomes like scattered dust, like a mirage, and like ashes, as in His saying: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [Al-Furqan: 23], and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾ [An-Nur: 39], and His saying: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes on which the wind blows hard on a stormy day﴾ [Ibrahim: 18]. Yet they believe that their deeds are good and accepted by Allah.

The correct view is that the verse was revealed concerning the disbelievers who believe that their disbelief is right and true, and that in it is the pleasure of their Lord. As He said about the idol-worshippers: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in position﴾ [Az-Zumar: 3], and He said about them: ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 18], and He said about the monks who draw near to Allah in a way not based on sound law: ﴿Faces that Day will be humbled, laboring and exhausted, entering a scorching fire﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 2–4], according to the view that these verses refer to them. His saying, may He be exalted, about the disbelievers: ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies rather than Allah, and they think they are guided﴾ [Al-A'raf: 30], and His saying: ﴿And indeed, they hinder them from the way, while they think they are guided﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 37]. The proof that it was revealed concerning the disbelievers is His explicit statement in the verse that follows it: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have become void﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105].

Therefore, the statement of whoever says they are the disbelievers, the statement of whoever says they are the monks, and the statement of whoever says they are the People of the Book who disbelieve in the Prophet (ﷺ), all of these are included in this verse. Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, that his son Mus'ab asked him about "the greatest losers in deeds" in this verse: "Are they the Harūriyyah (Kharijites)?" He said: "No, they are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ). As for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said there is no food in it nor drink." The Harūriyyah are those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation. Sa'd used to call them "the defiant ones" (al-fāsiqīn). End of quotation from al-Bukhari.

As for what is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that they are the people of Harura'—known as the Harūriyyah—its meaning is that some of the meaning of the verse applies to them according to what they did, because they commit abominable errors and believe that these are the meaning of the Book and the Sunnah. So their effort is lost while they think they are doing well, though they are, in this, less than open disbelievers, because the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specific cause, as we have already explained with its evidence.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿whose effort has been lost﴾ [Al-Kahf: 104] means that it became void and vanished. We have already stated that the word ḍalāl (going astray / loss) is used in the Qur'an and in the Arabic language in three senses:

The first: ḍalāl meaning departure from the path of truth to the path of falsehood, like departing from Islam to disbelief. This is its most common use in the Qur'an, and from it is His saying: ﴿Not the path of those who have earned Your anger, nor of those who are astray﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 7], and His saying: ﴿Do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the sound way﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 77].

The second: ḍalāl meaning destruction, disappearance and dissolution. From it is the Arabs' saying: "The ghee was lost in the food," when it is consumed in it and disappears in it. From it, in this sense, is His saying: ﴿And what they used to invent has vanished from them﴾ [Al-An'am: 24], that is, it disappeared and dissolved. His saying here: ﴿whose effort has been lost﴾ means that it became void and dissolved. And the poet's saying:

Did you not ask, so the dwellings would inform you about the tribe that became lost, where they went?

That is, about the tribe that disappeared and dissolved. From here burial is called iḍlāl (causing to go astray), because the end of the dead person buried is that his bones mix with the earth, so he is lost in it as ghee is lost in food. From the use of ḍalāl for burial is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

Those who buried him returned with a clear sign, and he was left in al-Jawlan, firm and bountiful.

His saying "mudilluhu" (those who buried him) means those who interred him in his grave. From this sense is His saying: ﴿And they say, "When we have become lost in the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ [As-Sajdah: 10]. The meaning of ﴿when we have become lost in the earth﴾ is that their decayed bones have mixed with it, so they disappeared and were consumed in it.

The third: ḍalāl meaning departure from knowledge of the reality of the matter, which corresponds to what is actually the case. From it, in this sense, is His saying: ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾ [Ad-Duha: 7], that is, unaware of the knowledge and insights you now know, which are not known except through revelation, so He guided you to those knowledge and insights through revelation. This sense is specified by His saying, of the sons of Ya'qub: ﴿They said, "By Allah, you are in your old error"﴾ [Yusuf: 95], that is, your departure from knowledge of the reality of Yusuf's affair. Because of this you hope for his return to you, and that has no hope, according to the most apparent interpretations. And His saying: ﴿But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the two errs [taḍilla iḥdāhumā]﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 282], that is, forgets the true knowledge of what was witnessed, through forgetfulness or the like, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿so that one of them may remind the other﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 282]. And His saying: ﴿He said, "Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets"﴾ [Taha: 52]. From this sense is the poet's saying:

And Salma thinks that I seek another in her place, while I see her wandering in error.

His saying "urāhā fi al-ḍalāl" (I see her in error) means in ignorance of the reality of the matter, since she thinks I seek another in her place, while the reality is otherwise.

His saying in this verse: ﴿while they think﴾ (yaḥsabūna), that is, they suppose. Some of the Seven Readers read it with a kasra on the sin, and some with a fatha, as we have stated many times throughout the Qur'an. The two objects of ḥasiba are the subject and predicate, on which inna acts, and the original is "they think themselves doing good in their work." His saying ṣun'an means work. Between "yaḥsabūna" (they think) and "yuḥsinūna" (they do well) is the paronomasia called by the rhetoricians tajnīs al-taṣḥīf (paronomasia of dotted letters), which is where the dots distinguish the two words, as in the saying of al-Buhturi:

The one deceived by Allah did not come by night to defeat, nor did the one who is strengthened by Allah seek him.

Between "al-mughtarr" (deceived) and "al-mu'tazz" (strengthened) is the paronomasia mentioned.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have become void﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105], is an explicit text that disbelief in the signs of Allah and in meeting Him voids deeds. The verses indicating this are very numerous, such as His saying in Al-'Ankabut: ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and meeting Him, those have despaired of My mercy, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 23]. Verses like this are very numerous, and some examples of that will come soon, if Allah wills.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al-Kahf: 105], has several interpretations among the scholars:

The first: the meaning is that they have no good deeds to be weighed in the other pan against their evil deeds. Rather, there were only evil deeds, and whoever is like that is in the Fire, as He said: ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves, in Hell they will abide forever. The Fire will burn their faces, and they therein will be grimacing﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 103–104]. And He said: ﴿The weighing that Day is the truth. So whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful. And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾ [Al-A'raf: 8–9]. And He said: ﴿As for one whose scales are light, his mother will be the Abyss. And what can make you know what that is? It is a Fire, blazing﴾ [Al-Qari'ah: 8–10], and other verses.

Some people of knowledge said: the meaning of ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ is that they have no value with Allah because of their insignificance, which is because of their disbelief. This is like His saying about them: ﴿They will enter Hell humiliated﴾ [Ghafir: 60], that is, abased, humbled, insignificant. And His saying: ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled"﴾ [As-Saffat: 18], and His saying: ﴿He said, "Remain therein in humiliation, and do not speak to Me"﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 108], and other verses indicating their degradation, lowliness and insignificance.

The authentic Sunnah has indicated that the meaning of the verse includes the disbelieving person who is large and corpulent, who will not weigh before Allah on the Day of Resurrection the wing of a mosquito. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, in explaining this verse: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, Abu al-Zinad related to me from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, a great, corpulent man will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh before Allah the wing of a mosquito." And he said: "Recite: ﴿So We will not give them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾." And from Yahya ibn Bukayr, from al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Zinad, the same. End of quotation from al-Bukhari.

This hadith is also narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, and it indicates that the soul of a fat, bloated disbeliever does not weigh the wing of a gnat before Allah. It also indicates the weighing of persons. Abu Abdullah al-Qurtubi, after mentioning the hadith of Abu Hurayra mentioned above, said in his tafsir of this verse the following text: "This hadith contains from the fiqh (jurisprudence) a condemnation of fatness for one who strives for it, because in that there is striving after foods and being preoccupied with them instead of noble pursuits. Rather, it indicates the prohibition of eating beyond the amount needed for sustenance, when the purpose is luxury and fattening. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Verily the most hated of men to Allah the Exalted is the fat rabbi (scholar).'" And from the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The best of you is my generation, then those who follow them." Imran said: "I do not know whether he mentioned after his generation two generations or three." "Then after you there will be a people who bear witness without being asked to bear witness, who betray and are not trusted, who make vows and do not fulfill them, and among whom fatness appears." This is a condemnation. The reason for this is that acquired fatness comes only from excessive eating, gluttony, ease, comfort, security, and indulging the self in its desires. Such a person is a slave to his self, not a slave to his Lord. Whoever is in this state will inevitably fall into what is forbidden, and every flesh that grew from unlawful gain, the Fire is more deserving of it. Allah the Exalted has condemned the disbelievers for excessive eating, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode﴾ [Muhammad: 12]. So if the believer resembles them, and indulges in their luxury in all his states and times, then where is the reality of faith and the upholding of the duties of Islam? Whoever eats and drinks much, his greed and avarice increase, and his laziness and sleep increase at night; so his day is spent in bewilderment and his night in sleep." End of quotation. The point of al-Qurtubi's speech is noted. However, what he included of asserting with certainty that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Verily Allah hates the fat rabbi" is open to scrutiny, because it has not been authentically established as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) report. Al-Bayhaqi graded it as hasan, but as a saying of Ka'b. What has been mentioned of the condemnation of excessive eating and drinking and of acquired fatness is evident, and its evidences are many. "Sufficient for the believer are a few morsels that keep his back upright."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 107:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Paradise (al-Firdaws) as a lodging (nuzulan)﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, majestic and exalted, mentions that faith and righteous deeds are the means of attaining the Gardens of al-Firdaws. The verses clarifying that righteous deeds are a cause of entering Paradise are very numerous, such as His statement, exalted is He: ﴿and give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward, [wherein they will remain forever]﴾ [al-Kahf: 2-3]; and His statement: ﴿And they will be called out, "This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do."﴾ [al-A'raf: 43], meaning: because of it; and His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And that is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 72]; and His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those will enter Paradise and not be wronged at all. [They will enter] Gardens of perpetual residence, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen﴾ [Maryam: 60-61], and other verses besides these.

Caution (tanbih)

If it is said: these verses indicate that obedience to Allah through faith and righteous deeds is a cause of entering Paradise, yet His statement (ﷺ): "None of you will enter Paradise by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace," there arises a problem concerning this.

The answer: a deed is not a cause of entering Paradise except when Allah accepts it, and His accepting it is from His grace. Thus the act which is a cause of entering Paradise is the one that Allah has accepted by His grace, and other deeds are not a cause of entering Paradise. There are other ways of reconciling the hadith with the mentioned verses, but this is the most apparent of them to me, and Allah knows best.

We have already mentioned that "nuzul" is what is prepared of honour for a guest or arrival.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 108:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Abiding therein forever; they will not desire any removal therefrom﴾.

That is: abiding forever in the Gardens of Firdaws, they will not desire any ḥiwal (ḥiwal: a removal, a transfer) from them, i.e., a transfer to another abode, because there is no abode better than them that one would desire to move to from them. Rather, they abide therein eternally without any transfer or relocation. (p-355) The meaning mentioned here is clarified in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence﴾ [Fatir: 35], i.e., of lasting residence forever; and His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward, in which they will remain forever﴾ [al-Kahf: 2–3]; and His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end﴾ [Sad: 54]; and His saying: ﴿A gift uninterrupted﴾ [Hud: 108], besides other verses that indicate their everlasting stay therein and the everlastingness of its bounties for them. And ḥiwal is a verbal noun (ism maṣdar) meaning taḥawwul (transfer).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 109:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted and Majestic commanded His Prophet ﷺ to say: ﴿If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 109], meaning: if the water of the sea were ink for the pens with which the words of Allah are written, ﴿the sea would surely be exhausted﴾, meaning: it would run out and come to an end, ﴿before the words of my Lord are exhausted﴾. ﴿And even if We brought the like of it as a supplement﴾, meaning: with another sea like it as a supplement, that is, an addition to it. His saying "madadan" (supplement) is in the accusative as a specification (tamyiz), and its i'rab (grammatical analysis) may also be taken as a circumstantial accusative (hal). This meaning has been further clarified in Surah Luqman in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if whatever trees on earth were pens and the sea, with seven more seas to supply it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman: 27]. These verses indicate that the words of Him, exalted is He, have no end, high is He above that by a great elevation.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 18, verse 110:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your god is but one God."﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to say to the people: ﴿I am only a human being like you﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. That is, I do not tell you that I am an angel or other than a human. Rather, I am a human being like you, meaning a human of the human species, except that Allah the Exalted has favoured me and singled me out with what He revealed to me of His Oneness and His law. His saying here, ﴿It has been revealed to me that your god is but one God﴾ [al-Kahf: 110], means: so affirm His oneness and do not associate anything with Him. What Allah has made clear in this verse He has explained further in other places, such as His saying at the beginning of Fussilat: ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your god is but one God. So take the straight path to Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to those who associate others with Allah, who do not give zakat and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter."﴾ [Fussilat: 6–7]. Also His saying: ﴿Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 93], and His saying: ﴿Say, "I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me"﴾ [al-An'am: 50], to the end of the verse.

What Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) in this verse, namely that he tell people that he is a human being, while Allah has favoured him over others with what He revealed to him, is similar to what came from the other Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, in His saying: ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only human beings like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants."﴾ [Ibrahim: 11]. That the Messengers are like human beings in that the origin and substance of all of them is one, and that the human attributes apply to all of them, does not conflict with their being preferred over the rest of mankind by what Allah has singled them out with of His revelation, their selection, and His preference for them, as is necessarily known.

Some scholars said: The meaning of this verse is: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists: ﴿I am only a human being like you﴾. So whoever among you claims that I am a liar, let him bring the like of what I have brought. For I do not know the unseen regarding what I have told you of the reports of past peoples that you asked about, such as the story of the People of the Cave and the account of Dhu al-Qarnayn. This view has its merit, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.﴾

His saying in this verse: ﴿whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110] includes his hoping for His reward and for seeing His noble Face on the Day of Resurrection, and his fearing His punishment. That is: whoever, hoping from his Lord on the day he meets Him for abundant reward and safety from evil, let him do righteous deeds.

We have already explained righteous and unrighteous deeds at the beginning of this noble surah and elsewhere, so there is no need to repeat it here.

As for His saying: ﴿and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, a group of scholars said: that is, he should not show off to people in his deed, because doing an act of worship of Allah for the sake of people's showing off is a kind of shirk (associating partners with Allah). As is known among scholars, riya' (showing off) is one of the kinds of shirk, and there are attributed hadiths about this, and Ibn Kathir cited parts of them in his tafsir of this verse. The verified view is that His saying: ﴿and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110] is more general than riya' and other things. That is: he should not worship his Lord for show and reputation, and he should not give any part of the rights of his Creator to any of His creatures. This is because Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him﴾ [al-Nisa': 48], in both places, and He says: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him away or the wind blew him into a distant place﴾ [al-Hajj: 31], along with other verses.

It is understood by the implication of the opposite of this noble verse that whoever associates anyone with his Lord in worship and does not do righteous deeds, does not hope for the meeting with his Lord, and whoever does not hope for the meeting with his Lord has no good with Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

This implication has been stated explicitly in other places, such as His saying mentioned just before: (﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in His meeting, so their deeds have become worthless, and We will not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection. That is their recompense: Hell﴾ [al-Kahf: 105–106]), because whoever disbelieves in the meeting with Allah does not hope for it. And His saying in al-'Ankabut: ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in His meeting — those have despaired of My mercy﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 23]; and His saying in al-A'raf: ﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter — their deeds have become worthless. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ [al-A'raf: 147]; and His saying in al-An'am: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, until when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾ [al-An'am: 31]; and His saying in Yunus: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not guided﴾ [Yunus: 45]; and His saying in al-Furqan: ﴿And those who do not hope for Our meeting say, "Why are the angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and have overstepped in insolence greatly﴾ [al-Furqan: 21]; and His saying in al-Rum: ﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought into punishment﴾ [al-Rum: 16], along with other verses.

* *

Note

Know that hope, as in His saying here, ﴿hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110], is used for hoping for good, and it is also used for fear. Its use for hoping for good is well known. Among the uses of hope for fear is the line of Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali:

When the bees sting him, the sting is not hoped for (i.e., not feared), and they have allied themselves with him in a house of wood, honey-bees.

His saying "lam yurja lasa'uha" means: its sting was not feared. It is also narrated as "halafaha" with ha' and kha', "'awasil" with sin, and "'awamil" with mim.

When you know that hope is applied to both of these meanings, know that they are mutually implied: whoever hopes for the good that is with Allah also fears the evil that is with Him, and vice versa. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this noble verse, namely His saying: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Kahf: 110].

On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, it was revealed concerning Jundub ibn Zuhayr al-Azdi al-Ghamidi, who said: O Messenger of Allah, I do deeds for Allah, the Exalted, and I want the Face of Allah, the Exalted, but when it is seen, it pleases me. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and He does not accept what has been associated with others in it." Then the verse was revealed. Al-Qurtubi mentioned it in his tafsir. Ibn Hajar mentioned in al-Isaba that it is from the narration of Ibn al-Kalbi in tafsir from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, and the weakness of this chain is well known.

On the authority of Tawus, he said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: I love jihad in the way of Allah, the Exalted, and I love that my position be seen. Then this verse was revealed.

On the authority of Mujahid, he said: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I give charity and maintain the ties of kinship, and I do not do that except for Allah, the Exalted. But it is mentioned about me, I am praised for it, and that pleases me, and I am impressed by it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent and said nothing. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. End of quotation from al-Qurtubi's tafsir.

It is known that whoever intends by his deed the Face of Allah does it for Allah, even if he is pleased by people's knowing of it, especially if his pleasure is for the sake of people following him in it. And whoever fights so that the word of Allah is supreme is in the way of Allah. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Sahib al-Durr al-Manthur said: Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾, that he said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists who worshipped another god alongside Allah, and it does not apply to the believers. 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Ikhlas, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim narrated from Tawus, who said: "A man said: O Prophet of Allah, I stand in positions seeking the Face of Allah, and I love that my station be seen. He did not answer him with anything until this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾." Al-Hakim narrated it and declared it sahih, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it connected from Tawus from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, who said: Among the Muslims there was one who fought while loving that his position be seen, so Allah revealed: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾. Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu'aym in al-Sahaba, and Ibn 'Asakir narrated through al-Suddi al-Saghir, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Jundub ibn Zuhayr, when he prayed, fasted, or gave charity and was mentioned with good, was pleased by it, so he increased in that because of people's talk, and Allah blamed him, and this verse was revealed concerning that: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾. Hannad in al-Zuhd narrated from Mujahid, who said: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I give charity and seek with it what is with Allah, but I love that it be said of me that I am good. So this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾." End of quotation from al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bil-Ma'thur. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.
